item.title: [newstribune.com] Late-game homers send Brewers past Dodgers, into 3-0 NLCS lead | Jefferson City News-Tribune
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla; Field Level Media
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Jake Bauers put his team’s determination on full display, getting the Milwaukee Brewers within one victory of their first World Series appearance in 44 years. Bauers turned an 11-pitch at-bat into a go-ahead two-run homer in the seventh inning as the Brewers took a commanding 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series with a 6-2 victory Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers. Milwaukee will aim for a sweep of the best-of-7 series tonight at Dodger Stadium. Garret
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- Jake Bauers put his team’s determination on full display, getting the Milwaukee Brewers within one victory of their first World Series appearance in 44 years.
Bauers turned an 11-pitch at-bat into a go-ahead two-run homer in the seventh inning as the Brewers took a commanding 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series with a 6-2 victory Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Milwaukee will aim for a sweep of the best-of-7 series tonight at Dodger Stadium.
Garrett Mitchell followed Bauers with a homer of his own as the Southern California natives put on a show in front of family and friends in a ballpark where the home team has played the bully for more than a decade.
“We play for each other. It’s as simple as that, man,” Bauers said. “Any time there’s a mistake, an error, a walk, pitchers give up runs, hitters strike out in a big spot, the only thing anybody’s thinking about is how can I help pick that guy up? How can I help pick that guy up and do my part to win this game?”
Rookie left-hander Robert Gasser gave up three hits over five scoreless innings as the Brewers moved closer to the franchise’s second trip to the World Series. The Brewers made their lone Fall Classic appearance in 1982 as an American League team, losing in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals.
Jackson Chourio led off the game with a first-pitch homer off Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell as Milwaukee showed its power capabilities after finishing last in the National League in homers during the regular season with 154.
“Job’s not finished yet,” Mitchell said. “Just got to take it a day at a time, not really worried about what’s happened today, what happened yesterday or what’s coming tomorrow. We’ve just got to show up and continue to play our brand of baseball and continue doing it for one another.”
Will Smith hit a two-run double for the Dodgers, who won the past two World Series titles. Los Angeles is trying to become the first National League club to win three consecutive Fall Classic championships.
Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts moved Shohei Ohtani to sixth in the batting order with the superstar in a postseason slump. Ohtani went 1-for-2 with a walk and a hit-by-pitch. The Dodgers’ offense was held to five hits in Game 3 after collecting three in Game 2.
“I haven’t digested this one,” Roberts said when asked about potential lineup changes for Game 4. “They’re going to run a bullpen game. Just trying to figure out which guys we want to be in there, how you kind of construct the lineup, but I haven’t thought about that one yet.”
Snell appeared to recover from Chourio’s ambush home run before he was rocked by consecutive home runs with no outs in the seventh. Snell (0-1) allowed four runs on four hits in six-plus innings with two walks and nine strikeouts.
“I just left the fastball over the middle to Bauers,” said Snell, who was in the Tampa Bay Rays organization with Bauers from 2015-18. “… I’ve seen the ups and downs he’s been through, and it’s been a lot of downs. So for him to go through this right now, he’s earned it. Hats off to him. What an at-bat.”
Trailing 1-0 from the jump, the Dodgers managed to put their leadoff batter on base in four of the first six innings before finally breaking through.
Gasser was replaced by right-hander Abner Uribe to open the sixth inning, and the reliever walked three of the first four batters he faced to load the bases, including a walk to Ohtani. Smith delivered a double off the wall in left-center field for a 2-1 lead after entering the game in a 1-for-25 slump.
Los Angeles failed to add onto the lead in the inning against left-hander DL Hall (3-0) when Enrique Hernandez and Tommy Edman struck out to end the threat.
Milwaukee responded immediately when Andrew Vaughn walked to open the seventh before Bauers’ epic at-bat. Two pitches later, Mitchell went over the wall in right-center field for a 4-2 advantage to end Snell’s outing.
Bauers had a similar plate appearance in Game 2 when he worked a 12-pitch walk with two outs in the third inning and Christian Yelich followed with a two-run single.
“Yeah, there was for sure a moment where I thought to myself like, ‘Oh, you’re in it again,’” Bauers said. “As far as the approach for the at-bat, I didn’t want to miss a fastball.”
The Brewers added to their lead in the eighth when Brice Turang scored on a Justin Wrobleski wild pitch, and Joey Ortiz tacked on an RBI single in the ninth.
Hall threw 2⅓ scoreless innings. Brewers closer Trevor Megill got the last four outs, striking out the final two batters, for his fourth save of the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers' Kyle Tucker makes 1 thing clear with LA facing NLCS elimination appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are one loss away from having their season end, but Kyle Tucker is not ready to write them off just yet. Los Angeles fell 6-2 to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series on Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, falling into a 3-0 series hole.
After the game, the star outfielder made it clear he still believes the Dodgers have what it takes to dig out of it.
"This team has won four games before, so that's what we're going to have to do," Tucker said. "I believe in this group, the staff, the clubhouse and guys in here. I think if there's a team to do it, it's this team, but it's not going to come easy, obviously."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"If there's a team to do it, it's this team."
Kyle Tucker on the #Dodgers facing a 3-0 series deficit in the #NLCS @CBSLosAngeles pic.twitter.com/45mwbGZhpU
— Sports Central LA (@SportsCentralLA) October 15, 2026
He also knows the Brewers are just as hungry. "They want to win as well, so we've just got to come out and get after it tomorrow," he said.
History is not on Los Angeles' side. The 2004 Boston Red Sox remain the only team in MLB history to win a best-of-seven postseason series after falling behind 3-0, rallying past the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series. The Dodgers themselves have trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series only once before, when the Baltimore Orioles swept them in the 1966 World Series.
Still, there is a reason Tucker has faith in this group. The Dodgers are the two-time defending World Series champions, and they swept these same Brewers in four games in last year's NLCS. Tucker joined the club this past offseason on a four-year, $240 million deal.
To keep that run alive, the offense will have to wake up quickly. The Dodgers have scored only seven runs in three games, have yet to hit a home run in the series, and have struggled badly with runners in scoring position all postseason.
Milwaukee, meanwhile, has done almost everything right. Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back home runs in the seventh inning to flip Game 3, and the Brewers' bullpen has been nearly untouchable throughout October.
The Dodgers will try to stave off elimination in Game 4 on Thursday at Dodger Stadium, with the Brewers aiming to clinch their first National League pennant.
Related: Dodgers' Miguel Rojas calls out glaring culprit behind LA's 3-0 NLCS hole

The 2026 MLB playoffs are in full swing!
The 12-team postseason began with an action-packed wild-card round that featured eight teams battling for four spots to advance to the eight-team division series.
The Chicago White Sox became the first team to win a series this postseason with a wild-card round sweep of the Houston Astros. Then the New York Yankees swept the Boston Red Sox in two routs, recording the highest series run differential in the history of the current wild-card format. The San Diego Padresalso sealed their spot in the NLDS with a sweep of the Chicago Cubs. In the only wild-card series to go the distance, the Atlanta Braves held off the Philadelphia Philliesto move on.
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Braves to nab the first spot in the championship series, where they are facing the Milwaukee Brewers after they beat the Padres.
The Tampa Bay Rays swept the Yankees to clinch the first spot in the ALCS and face the Cleveland Guardians, who mounted a stunning comeback against the White Sox after dropping the first two games of the ALDS.
From the first pitch of the wild-card games to the last out of the World Series, we've got you covered with the postseason bracket, schedules, results and how to watch every game this October.

item.dc:creator: Michael DeRosa
item.description: The New York Yankees once again failed to win the World Series this year after having high expectations. After sweeping the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card series, the Yankees got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. Due to this, New York should be aiming to strengthen their roster this offseason. One major need that the Yankees have heading into the offseason is another impactful power hitter. Because of this, they are now being urged to sign one of this year's top free agents from the C
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees once again failed to win the World Series this year after having high expectations.
After sweeping the Boston Red Sox in the AL Wild Card series, the Yankees got swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS. Due to this, New York should be aiming to strengthen their roster this offseason.
One major need that the Yankees have heading into the offseason is another impactful power hitter. Because of this, they are now being urged to sign one of this year's top free agents from the Chicago Cubs.
New York Yankees Urged to Sign Cubs Star
Joe Najarian of SI.com urged the Yankees to sign Cubs star outfielder Seiya Suzuki this offseason in a recent article.
"But after his injury-plagued season, Judge will inevitably be limited to DH duties in the future. And given how good Suzuki was in 2026, the Yankees' post-Judge outfield would be in very good shape if they sign the Japanese slugger," Najarian wrote.
With the Yankees needing another star outfielder, it is understandable that they are being linked to him. He would certainly be a big addition to the Yankees' roster if signed. This is because he has shown throughout his career that he is a star.
Suzuki just had an impressive season with the Cubs, too. In 143 games in 2026, he recorded 26 home runs, 86 RBI, and a .270 batting average. This is after he had 32 home runs and 103 RBI in 2025 with Chicago. With numbers like these, he certainly would give New York's roster more pop if signed.
Should the Yankees Make This Move?
With Suzuki being a star, it would make a lot of sense for New York to sign Suzuki. Landing Suzuki would be massive for a Yankees club that wants to have better success in 2027. This is because he is a very impactful player when playing at his best and could thrive in New York.
Suzuki is exactly the kind of player that a contender like the Yankees should be adding, too. He has been consistently good at the plate and would simply make New York a more difficult team to go up against.
The Yankees will have a ton of competition to land Suzuki, though. This is because he is not only coming off a great season but is one of this year's top pending free agents. Thus, he will generate a lot of interest around the league. This will only heighten his value.
Although this is the case, it still makes sense for the Yankees to sign Suzuki. They need to win a World Series during the Judge era. Due to this, they are in a position to make a splash for Suzuki.
This article was originally published on HEAVY

item.dc:creator: Jared Greenspan; Max Ralph

item.content:encoded:
After setting a franchise record with an MLB-best 103 wins in the 2026 regular season, the Brewers are vying for their first World Series appearance since 1982, which remains the only trip to the fall classic in franchise history.
Chourio pounced on the first pitch of Game 3 of the National League Championship Series from Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell, parking it over the right-center-field fence for a home run. It was his sixth career postseason dinger at just 22 years old, breaking a tie with Contreras -- who has three long balls in the 2026 playoffs -- for the most in Brewers postseason history.
With both in mind, who is each team’s all-time postseason home run king? Here’s a breakdown of the players who hold a franchise’s playoff home run record.
American League East
Blue Jays: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. -- 8
Vladdy put together one of the single greatest individual postseason performances we’ve ever seen in 2025, leading the Blue Jays all the way to Game 7 of the World Series. After starting his postseason career with six homer-less games, Guerrero hit all eight of his October long balls in ‘25. He surpassed José Bautista (six) for the most home runs in Blue Jays playoff history. The dinger that earned Guerrero the franchise lead came off of Shohei Ohtani in the World Series, no less.
Orioles: Frank Robinson -- 9
The Hall of Famer had a knack for the clutch. Robinson's 26 career walk-off hits (regular season and postseason) are the most by any player since RBI became official in 1920. That knack extended to the playoffs, where Robinson posted an .887 OPS and slammed 10 total homers, including a franchise-best nine with the Orioles. Robinson won World Series MVP in 1966 after hitting go-ahead home runs in Games 1 and 4 of a Baltimore sweep over the Dodgers.
Rays: Randy Arozarena -- 11
Arozarena put the Rays on his back in the 2020 postseason, recording 29 hits -- at the time the most in a single postseason. Ten of those hits were home runs, giving Arozarena another single-postseason record and pulling him ahead of Evan Longoria (nine) for the most playoff homers in Rays franchise history. Oh, and Arozarena did all of this as a rookie. He tagged one more postseason big fly with the Rays in '21 before joining the Mariners via trade in 2024.
Red Sox: David Ortiz -- 17
Big Papi was an October legend in the truest sense of the phrase. His walk-off heroics helped the Red Sox overcome a 3-0 series deficit in the 2004 ALCS, paving the way for a curse-breaking World Series title. Ortiz’s 17 playoff home runs included two walk-offs and six with the Red Sox facing elimination.
Yankees: Bernie Williams -- 22
Williams played in the postseason in 12 consecutive years from 1995-2006, with huge moments at several turns. His 1996 performance -- an 1.142 OPS with six homers -- is one of the best postseasons of all time. Overall, his 22 long balls are fifth most by any player in playoff history, sharing a list with other Yankees legends like Derek Jeter (20) and Mickey Mantle (18).
AL Central
Guardians: Jim Thome -- 17
Thome hit all 17 of his postseason homers with Cleveland. He’s one of three players with multiple postseason grand slams, along with Francisco Lindor and Jason Varitek. Thome's grand slams came in Game 6 of the 1998 ALCS against the Yankees and Game 2 of the 1999 ALDS against the Red Sox.
Royals: George Brett -- 10
Brett is one of just 12 players who have hit three home runs in a single postseason game. His herculean effort came in Game 3 of the 1978 ALCS against the Yankees. Even though in defeat, Brett memorably whacked three pitches over the fence, one out to left field, one over the center-field fence, and one to right field.
Tigers: Miguel Cabrera -- 9
Cabrera’s most memorable postseason may have come as a rookie with the championship-winning Marlins in 2003 (more on that soon). But his most impactful playoff performance happened in 2011, when he launched four home runs with a 1.261 OPS in 11 games for the Tigers. He later passed Delmon Young’s eight career playoff home runs as a Tiger with a solo shot in Game 1 of the 2014 ALDS.
Twins: Kirby Puckett -- 5
Goose Goslin is the Twins' franchise leader in postseason home runs with seven, but Puckett holds the record since the club moved to Minnesota in 1961. Puckett took two trips to the postseason with the Twins, winning the World Series both times (1987 and 1991). The Hall of Famer was particularly impactful in ‘91, when he hit four dingers on an overall .333/.396/.667 slash line. That included an iconic 11th-inning walk-off homer in Game 6 of the Fall Classic.
White Sox: Paul Konerko -- 7
Konerko mashed five of his seven postseason homers during Chicago's 2005 title run, narrowly besting teammate Paul Crede (four HR) for the franchise lead. Konerko hit two of his long balls while earning ALCS MVP honors, then later launched a go-ahead grand slam in Game 2 of the World Series to down the Astros.
AL West
Angels: Troy Glaus -- 9
Glaus hit seven of his nine postseason homers with the Angels during the club's World Series campaign in 2022. Three of those were go-ahead long balls in the sixth inning or later, which is tied with the Astros' Yordan Alvarez (2022) for the most such home runs in a single postseason.
Athletics: José Canseco -- 7
In addition to holding the club's all-time postseason home run record, Canseco holds a share of the record for the most homers in a single postseason by an A's player. He slugged four big flies in 1988, helping lead the Athletics to the AL Pennant. Two years later, Canseco passed Al Simmons for the most postseason home runs in A's franchise history with a dinger in Game 2 of the 1990 World Series.
Astros: Jose Altuve -- 28
Altuve added to his stature as one of baseball's best postseason hitters in 2026. He clubbed a solo shot in Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series against the White Sox, putting him one home run behind Manny Ramirez for most all-time. And Altuve tends to meet the moment, too: A whopping 14 of his playoff homers have been of the game-tying or go-ahead variety, the most such homers in postseason history.
Mariners: Jay Buhner and Edgar Martinez -- 8
Buhner and Martinez each starred for the Mariners during the most successful era in franchise history, as the club made the playoffs four times between 1994 and 2001. Buhner took the early lead in career postseason homers, hitting four in ‘95 and two more in ‘97. But Martinez caught up to his longtime teammate in 2001 with a pair of long balls in the 2001 ALDS.
Rangers: Nelson Cruz -- 14
Cruz authored a historic postseason moment when he hit the first walk-off grand slam in postseason history in Game 2 of the 2011 ALCS against the Tigers. It remains one of just two walk-off postseason slams after Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman also accomplished the feat in Game 1 of the 2024 World Series. Cruz, the owner of 464 regular-season home runs, hit his last postseason homer at age 41 with the Rays, becoming the second-oldest player to go yard in a playoff game.
National League East
Braves: Chipper Jones -- 13
Jones starred for an Atlanta team that made 11 consecutive postseason appearances from 1995-2005. The eight-time All-Star broke onto the October stage in a big way in ‘95, slugging two home runs -- including the game-winning shot in the ninth inning -- in a 5-4 win over the Rockies in Game 1 of the NLDS. Jones and Austin Riley are the only two players in Braves history with multiple go-ahead homers in the eighth inning or later of a postseason game.
Marlins: Miguel Cabrera -- 4
A 20-year-old, baby-faced Cabrera looked at home in his first postseason in 2003, steering the Florida Marlins to the franchise’s second World Series title. Cabrera launched four home runs in the ‘03 playoffs -- his only with the Marlins -- which stands as the most home runs in a single postseason at age 20 or younger in MLB history. With a long ball off Yankees right-hander Roger Clemens in Game 4 of the World Series, Cabrera became the second youngest player to go yard in the Fall Classic.
Mets: Daniel Murphy -- 7
All seven of Murphy’s playoff home runs with the Mets came during a magical two-week stretch in 2015. The second baseman homered in six straight postseason games -- spanning Game 4 of the NLDS through Game 4 of the NLCS -- to steer the Mets to the NL Pennant. That’s the longest streak in a single postseason in MLB history. Even more impressive, Murphy homered off three former Cy Young winners: Clayton Kershaw, Zack Greinke and Jake Arrieta.
Nationals: Bryce Harper, Juan Soto, Anthony Rendon and Ryan Zimmerman -- 5
Four of the most iconic players in Nationals franchise history (since the team moved from Montreal to Washington) share this distinction. Youth is a popular theme here. At 19 years old and 362 days, Harper became the second-youngest player in MLB history to homer in a postseason game when he went deep in Game 5 of the 2012 NLDS. Seven years later, Soto (20 years, 346 days) became the sixth-youngest player to homer in the playoffs, teeing off for a two-run shot in Game 3 of the 2019 NLDS.
Phillies: Kyle Schwarber -- 13
Schwarber is one of the most prolific power hitters in playoff history: His 24 career playoff home runs rank third most all time, trailing only Ramirez and Altuve. He’s crushed 15 homers in a Phillies uniform, the latest being a 447-foot shot in Game 2 of the 2026 NL Wild Card Series against the Braves. In 2022, Schwarber keyed a stirring run to the World Series with three home runs in the NLCS against the Padres and three more dingers in the Fall Classic against the Astros.
NL Central
Brewers: Jackson Chourio -- 6
Chourio tattooed a pair of home runs to help the Brewers stave off elimination in Game 2 of the 2024 NL Wild Card Series, becoming the second-youngest player in postseason history with a multi-HR game (20 years & 205 days). He’s the only player in postseason history with a leadoff home run under age 22 -- which he’s done three times -- and the only player in MLB history with six playoff home runs before turning 23. Chourio's leadoff dinger off Blake Snell in Game 3 of the NLCS against the Dodgers as his latest feat of strength.
Cardinals: Albert Pujols -- 13
Who else but The Machine? Pujols slugged 19 career playoff home runs -- T-7th most all time -- including 13 with the Cardinals. The future Hall of Famer tagged Randy Johnson for his first career playoff homer in Game 2 of the 2001 NLDS, a surefire sign of things to come. Pujols is one of just 12 players to go deep three times in a postseason game, doing so in Game 3 of the 2011 World Series. He also launched one of the most iconic home runs in franchise history with a go-ahead, three-run shot onto the train tracks in Houston off All-Star closer Brad Lidge in Game 5 of the 2005 NLCS.
Cubs: Kris Bryant, Anthony Rizzo and Kyle Schwarber -- 6
Talk about a fitting trio: These three All-Stars propelled the Cubs to a curse-breaking, legacy-defining World Series title in 2016. Bryant (2) and Rizzo (1) each launched home runs in the Fall Classic, keying victories in Games 5 and 6 to spur a historic 3-1 series comeback. Schwarber, one of the best postseason power hitters of all time, launched six of his 24 playoff homers with the Cubs, including five dingers in his introduction to playoff baseball in 2015.
Pirates: Willie Stargell -- 7
The Hall of Fame slugger managed just two home runs while hitting .217 across his first 26 postseason games, spanning five different playoff appearances. But Stargell flipped the script in his age-39 season in 1979, smashing five home runs while earning NLCS and World Series MVP honors. Stargell’s two-run blast in the sixth inning of Game 7 of the ‘79 World Series proved to be the World Series-winning hit.
Reds: Johnny Bench -- 10
Bench played in 10 postseason series across his illustrious 17-year career and, rather remarkably, homered in all but one of them -- only going without a long ball in the 1975 NLCS. The Hall of Fame catcher’s only multi-HR playoff series came in the 1976 Fall Classic, when he swatted a pair of homers, posted a 1.667 OPS and took home World Series MVP honors for the Big Red Machine.
NL West
D-backs: Chris Young -- 5
Young only played in 12 postseason games for Arizona, but that was plenty of time to rewrite the franchise record books. His leadoff home run in Game 3 of the 2007 NLDS against the Cubs’ Rich Hill accounts for the only leadoff home run in D-backs franchise history. Four years later, Young slammed a pair of long balls in Game 4 of the NLDS against the Brewers. It remains the only multi-HR game by a Diamondbacks’ hitter in franchise history.
Dodgers: Max Muncy -- 19
Muncy homered three times in the 2026 NLDS against the Braves, pushing his total to 19 playoff home runs and extending the most in Dodgers postseason history. It’s a remarkable record for Muncy to hold, given his journey: He first joined the Dodgers organization on a Minor League contract in 2017, after he was released by the Athletics. The three-time All-Star owns some of the most important home runs in Dodgers history. That includes his 18th-inning walk-off in Game 3 of the 2018 World Series and his eighth-inning home run in Game 7 of the 2025 Fall Classic, which set the stage for a stirring late-game comeback.
Giants: Barry Bonds -- 8
Bonds made the postseason only four times in 15 seasons with the Giants. And while he launched more home runs (756) than anyone in baseball history, Bonds actually was held without a home run in three of those four trips to October. All eight of his playoff home runs with San Francisco came in 2002, when he posted a 1.559 OPS in 17 games while leading the Giants to the NL Pennant. The most memorable occurred in the ninth inning of Game 2 of the World Series, when he clobbered a blast to right field off closer Troy Percival. Arozarena (10, 2020 Rays) is the only player with more home runs in a single postseason.
Padres: Manny Machado -- 9
Machado extended his own franchise record in his first at-bat of the 2026 postseason, launching a home run in the first inning of Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series against the Cubs’ Matthew Boyd. Machado ushered in a new era of baseball in San Diego when he signed a 10-year deal ahead of the 2019 season, and the Padres have made the playoffs in five of the eight years since. The seven-time All-Star was at his best in the 2022 playoffs, helping San Diego win a pair of postseason series thanks to four home runs in 12 games.
Rockies: Matt Holliday -- 5
Holliday is responsible for one of the defining moments in Rockies history, although it has nothing to do with a home run: He belly-flopped into home plate to score the game-winning run in Game 163 in 2007, giving Colorado the Wild Card tiebreaker over San Diego. That mad dash set the stage for Holliday's only postseason stint with the club, which was wildly successful. The seven-time All-Star homered in each of his first two playoff games in the NLDS against the Phillies, and wound up with five long balls as the Rockies earned the franchise’s first World Series berth.

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers hold a 2-0 series lead in the NLCS against the Los Angeles Dodgers entering Wednesday night as the series shifts to L.A.
Left-hander Robert Gasser will take the mound for the Brewers, while the Dodgers will send out lefty Blake Snell.
With Snell on the mound, Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy has made a sudden change to his starting lineup from Game 2.
Brewers Announce Christian Yelich Move
While most of the lineup will remain similar to what’s been working for them, Murphy has elected not to start veteran Christian Yelich.
Yelich has been a major part of the Brewers’ success this season and so far in October. However, he’s taken on more of a platoon role when left-handed pitchers take the mound.
We saw that in Game 1 when the Dodgers sent out Tarik Skubal. Yelich didn’t start that game. However, he hit fifth in the lineup in Game 2 and recorded two hits and two RBIs in the team’s 7-4 win.
Via Underdog MLB: “Brewers 10/14 J. Chourio LF B. Turang 2B W. Contreras C A. Vaughn DH J. Bauers 1B G. Mitchell CF C. Pratt SS L. Lara RF J. Ortiz 3B R. Gasser SP.”
Brewers 10/14
J. Chourio LF
B. Turang 2B
W. Contreras C
A. Vaughn DH
J. Bauers 1B
G. Mitchell CF
C. Pratt SS
L. Lara RF
J. Ortiz 3B
R. Gasser SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) October 14, 2026
Yelich’s 2026 Season With Brewers
In his 14th MLB season, Yelich has had to take a step back from being a surefire everyday player.
He rarely plays the field anymore, and that honestly fits the Brewers’ current roster.
Milwaukee has a plethora of players who fill different roles, which is a big reason the team finished the regular season with the best record in baseball and sits just two wins away from winning the National League and reaching the World Series.
Yelich has appeared in 118 games and is hitting .235 with 69 runs, 104 hits, 12 home runs and 59 RBIs.
In the postseason, he’s recorded at least one hit in every game, going 8-for-19 at the plate with two walks.

item.content:encoded:
In early August, the Detroit Tigers put to rest any idea of extending ace pitcher Tarik Skubal, who was dealt to the Los Angeles Dodgers in return for a trio of prospects, which included pitcher River Ryan.
While the Tigers unfortunately failed to earn a spot in the MLB postseason, the Dodgers are back in the National League Championship Series once again. And Skubal is attempting to help the club become the first team in over a quarter-century to win three straight World Series titles.
Former Detroit Tigers Pitcher Tarik Skubal Comes Clean On Heavy Expectations
Given his status as one of the premier players at his position in baseball, along with what the Dodgers are trying to accomplish, Skubal is well aware of the heavy expectations that he’s facing.
However, he made it clear that he embraces it.
“The pressure surrounding the Dodgers is a privilege. As an athlete, this is what you want to be and you want to have an expectation to win,” Skubal said to Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez.
“I have those same expectations as a player and in my shoes, I think just keeping the game the game, going out there and competing and doing what I can to put my team in a position to win is important.”
Despite a good performance on the mound against the Brewers in Game 1 of the NLCS, Skubal was credited with the loss; his next starting opportunity is Game 5, but he and his teammates currently trail two games to none.
It Was Not Easy For The Tigers To Lose Tarik Skubal
Shortly after the trade of Skubal to the Dodgers was completed, Tigers manager A.J. Hinch admitted that it wasn’t easy despite having been preparing for that potential outcome.
“We’ve been bracing for something like this to happen,” Hinch said of the trade via the Detroit News. “Even though we’ve been talking about it for a couple of months, it’s still tough when it becomes a reality. But these guys are pretty resilient.”
“It’s been incredible to watch this guy rise to the top of the sport,” Hinch said. “He carried us a lot and I am forever grateful that our paths crossed. And for the things he did for this organization and the two playoff teams. His presence, his work ethic, his example, his dominance, there’s just so much to go through. But I am very grateful I was able to manage him for the time I did.”

item.title: [Front Office Sports] As Dodgers’ NLCS Hopes Fade, Game 3 Ticket Prices Drop
item.dc:creator: Eric Fisher
item.description: The Dodgers’ bid for MLB’s first three-peat championship in 26 years is fading, and the ticket resale market shows that emerging reality. The National League Championship Series shifts to Los Angeles for Game 3 on Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, with the Brewers holding a commanding 2–0 lead. In two rollicking games at American Family Field, Milwaukee came back from early deficits in both contests to win, and gave Los Angeles its biggest postseason series deficit since being swept by Arizona in the
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers’ bid for MLB’s first three-peat championship in 26 years is fading, and the ticket resale market shows that emerging reality.
The National League Championship Series shifts to Los Angeles for Game 3 on Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, with the Brewers holding a commanding 2–0 lead. In two rollicking games at American Family Field, Milwaukee came back from early deficits in both contests to win, and gave Los Angeles its biggest postseason series deficit since being swept by Arizona in the 2023 NL Division Series.
As fans’ confidence in the team declines, so have ticket prices. The get-in price on the resale market for Game 3 has fallen to $97 per ticket, down by 42% compared to Monday, according to TicketData. Tickets to Thursday’s Game 4 are down by 37% over the past three days to a $98 get-in price.
“We’ve just got to win [Wednesday],” Dodgers Manager Dave Roberts said. “It’s not the position we expected to be in. [The Brewers] have a very good ball club. They’ve earned those two wins. We’ve got to win. So I don’t think it’s any more simple than that.”
The Dodgers have been MLB’s most-attended team for the past 13 years, and regularly fill the league’s largest stadium, so any relative softness in the team’s ticket market is noteworthy.
Conversely, hopes are rising for the Brewers reaching their first World Series since 1982. Get-in resale pricing for a potential World Series Game 1 in Milwaukee on Oct. 23 stands at $1,122 per ticket, up by 2% since Monday.
On betting markets, the Brewers have an implied probability of 74% of winning the NLCS.
Ohtani Watch
Part of the Dodgers’ struggles center on designated hitter Shohei Ohtani. The superstar hasn’t pitched since early July, and he recently came back from a stay on the injured list due to right bicep and left knee issues.
Ohtani, however, still isn’t fully healthy, and has struggled badly at the plate. In the postseason, he’s batted just .150 and has no extra-base hits. That has extended a slump in which he’s hit just .197 in his last 35 games, and since Aug. 18, he has no home runs and has driven in just one run.
“The symptoms shouldn’t be the reason why I can’t hit,” Ohtani said Thursday through interpreter Will Ireton.
The Dodgers briefly considered benching Ohtani for Game 3 of the NLCS to give him additional rest, but he is expected to be in the lineup. Already in the postseason, Ohtani has been dropped multiple times in the batting order.
“In this big moment, we’re listening to Shohei, and we’re going to support the crap out of him and believe in him, and that’s it,” Roberts said.

item.description: On March 26, Dave Roberts embarked on his 11th season as manager of the Los Angeles Dodgers. With expectations higher than ever coming off back-to-back World Series titles, no one was more prepared than Doc. But that would be put to the test following a 7-4 loss on Monday to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 2 of the National League Championship Series. item.content:encoded:
On March 26, Dave Roberts embarked on his 11th season as manager of the Los Angeles Dodgers.
With expectations higher than ever coming off back-to-back World Series titles, no one was more prepared than Doc. But that would be put to the test following a 7-4 loss on Monday to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 2 of the National League Championship Series.
Down 2-0, Roberts faced his toughest managerial decision: the possibility of benching Shohei Ohtani in a pivotal Game 3.
After much deliberation, it goes the way of Ohtani as he will be in the starting lineup for Game 3 of the NLCS, Roberts told reporters on Tuesday, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic.
Dodgers will find order spot for Ohtani
He will hit between two or sixth in the batting order.
There's no doubt that Ohtani has yet to recover from his ailing left knee or right bicep issues that plagued him during the last few months of the regular season. All that culmination forced the hand of the Dodgers to place him on the Injured List and, in return, call up Josue De Paula — who's brought to the 100-win ballclub in his short arrival.
Still, Ohtani himself was very "adamant" that he was healthy enough to contribute to the team and was not pinning any blame on his injuries as the reason he couldn't get it going at the plate, per Ardaya, thus persuading Roberts in his decision.
"In this big moment, we're listening to Shohei. And we're supporting the crap out of him and believe in him," Roberts said.
Despite a slashline of .150/.261/.150 and an OPS of .411 in six postseason games thus far, the Dodgers will continue to roll with the four-time MVP.
Ohtani OK with his swing right now
Ohtani himself feels that his swing is in a good spot and believes that he is close to breaking out of his egregious slump. But he'll have to figure it out with the Brewers' starting rotation turning to southpaw Roberts Gasser in Game 3.
"The symptoms have subdued a lot. Especially when I was on the IL, spending that time to be able to reduce the symptoms," Ohtani said about where his swing is and how he's managed that buildup with his injuries.
Following Monday's loss, Katie Woo and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reported that Roberts was putting all cards on the table when it came to how the Game 3 lineup would look.
That included the chance of benching Ohtani and having him replaced in the designated hitter spot with De Paula.
De Paula will remain a steady bat off the bench as Ohtani continues battling through a rough stretch with the Dodgers' season and three-peat hopes hanging in the balance.

item.title: [PCMag] Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians Livestream: How to Watch Today's MLB Championship Game, Even for Free
item.dc:creator: Jason Cohen
item.description: As summer comes to a close and the air turns crisp, you know what's coming: the MLB Playoffs. The NFL season is already underway, and if you're also a baseball lover, this next month is essential viewing. The MLB has been through a number of changes in recent years. From the universal DH and the pitch clock to video replay and an automated strike zone, baseball may look very different if you haven't been paying attention. item.content:encoded:
As summer comes to a close and the air turns crisp, you know what's coming: the MLB Playoffs. The NFL season is already underway, and if you're also a baseball lover, this next month is essential viewing. The MLB has been through a number of changes in recent years. From the universal DH and the pitch clock to video replay and an automated strike zone, baseball may look very different if you haven't been paying attention.
This week, the Dodgers will go head-to-head against the Brewers, and the Guardians will face the Rays in the best-of-seven Championship series. Which teams will come out on top? Here's how you can watch live.
What Time Is the Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians Game?
Today's game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers will take place on Tuesday, October 13 at 8 p.m. ET.
How to Watch the Tampa Bay Rays vs. Cleveland Guardians?
American League Division Series games will be broadcast on TBS, while National League games will be on Fox and FS1. You can also watch them with a live TV or sports streaming subscription from DirecTV, Fox One, Fubo, HBO Max, Hulu, Sling, Sportsnet+ (if you're in Canada), or YouTube TV.
How to Watch the Rays vs. the Guardians for Free
If you don't want to subscribe to any of the above platforms, you may be able to sign up for a few free trials to gain access to this weekend's games. Fox One and Hulu offer three-day trials, DirecTV and Fubo offer five days, and YouTube TV gives you 10 days for free.
2026 MLB Playoffs Game Schedule
MLB's expanded postseason means more teams on the playoff schedule. Things started off with the best-of-three Wild Card Series, where the Braves, Padres, White Sox, and Yankees advanced. The best-of-five Division Series put them up against the Los Angeles Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers, Cleveland Guardians, and Tampa Bay Rays, respectively. All of whom managed to advance
Now, the Rays and Guardians and Dodgers and Brewers meet in the best-of-seven Championship Series to determine the best team in each league. The winner from each league will then advance to a best-of-seven World Series to begin on October 23. Who will make it all the way?
Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Milwaukee Brewers - MIL lead 2-0
- Game 3 on October 14 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1
- Game 4 on October 15 @ 9 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1
- Game 5 on October 16 @ 9 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
- Game 6 on October 18 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
- Game 7 on October 19 @ 8 p.m. ET - Fox/FS1*
Cleveland Guardians vs. Tampa Bay Rays - CLE leads 1-0
- Game 2 on October 13 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 3 on October 15 @ 6 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 4 on October 16 @ 6 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max
- Game 5 on October 17 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
- Game 6 on October 19 @ 5 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
- Game 7 on October 20 @ 8 p.m. ET - TBS/HBO Max*
*if necessary
How to Stream the 2026 MLB Playoffs
This year's MLB postseason is stretched across multiple networks and streaming services. All Wild Card Series games for the American League and National League were broadcast on NBC, NBCSN, and Peacock. Additional rounds will be on other networks. ALDS and ALCS games are on TBS/TruTV and HBO Max, while NLDS and NLCS games are on Fox/FS1. For the World Series, all games will be broadcast on Fox and the Fox One streaming service.
- DirecTV: DirecTV's MySports base pack costs $45 per month for the first six months to see every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, and TBS/TruTV.
- Fox One: Fox's own streaming app lets you watch the NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox and FS1 for $20 per month.
- Fubo: Fubo's Sports plan costs $45.99 for the first month to watch the Wild Card Series, NLDS, NLCS, and World Series on Fox, FS1, and NBC/NBCSN.
- HBO Max: If you pay for the $18.49-per-month HBO Max Standard, you'll be able to watch the ALDS and ALCS games on TBS/TruTV.
- Hulu: For $90 per month, you can watch every game on Fox, FS1, NBC, TBS, and TruTV.
- Peacock: Instead of a live TV service, you'd need to pay $10.99 per month for Peacock Premium to see the Wild Card Series games.
- Sling: The $60.99-per-month Sling Orange & Blue bundle will let you watch the ALDS and ALCS on TBS/TruTV and the NLDS and NLCS on FS1. Day Passes are also available for Sling Orange, allowing you to watch games on TBS for up to seven days.
- Sportsnet+ (Canada only): The $30-per-month Standard tier lets you watch every postseason game.
- YouTube TV: Though the standard plan for YouTube TV costs $83 per month, you can actually now pay for the cheaper $65 Sports package to see all games on Fox, FS1, NBC/NBCSN, and TBS/TruTV.
Can I Watch Postseason Games on MLB.TV?
Are you already an MLB.TV subscriber? You can watch the Division Series, Championship Series, and World Series games through MLB's own streaming service—but there's a catch. To watch on MLB.TV, you'll first need to authenticate through a participating pay TV provider. It's such a sticking point that it makes the entire question moot. If you already have a TV provider, then you wouldn't need to use a streaming service. If you don't already have an MLB.TV subscription, don't pay for one now.
How can I listen to the 2026 postseason?
You can also listen to the games via ESPN Radio.
Which Teams Are In the Playoffs?
Since MLB expanded its postseason picture in 2022, a total of 12 teams make the playoffs each year. That includes six teams per league, including the three division winners and three Wild Card teams.
- American League Division Winners: Tampa Bay Rays (1), Cleveland Guardians (2), Houston Astros (3)
- American League Wild Card: New York Yankees (4), Boston Red Sox (5), Chicago White Sox (6)
- National League Division Winners: Milwaukee Brewers (1), Los Angeles Dodgers (2), Atlanta Braves (3)
- National League Wild Card: Chicago Cubs (4), Philadelphia Phillies (5), San Diego Padres (6)
Upgrade Your Streaming Experience
If you decide to watch the MLB postseason, there's still time to get a big-screen television for viewing this beautiful game. Pro tip: Turn on your TV's motion-smoothing option for the best picture while watching sports. Just remember to turn it off before watching other TV shows and movies to avoid the awful "soap opera" effect.
About Our Expert
As PCMag's editor of how to content, I have to cover a wide variety of topics and also make our stories accessible to everyday users. Considering my history as a technical writer, copywriter, and all-around freelancer covering baseball, comics, and more at various outlets, I am used to making myself into an expert.
I believe tech corporations are bad, but you might as well know how to use technology in everyday life. Want more how to content delivered right to your inbox? Sign up for the tips and tricks newsletter that I curate three times a week.
My job as how-to guru means I use just about every gadget under the sun, so I can figure out how everything works. I work from a Lenovo ThinkPad running Windows 11, but also have a very large Dell Inspiron 17 3000 and Apple silicon MacBook. I have a Google Pixel 6a for personal use and use a Galaxy Z Flip 4 for additional Samsung-related testing. For iOS coverage, an iPhone 13 mini works like a charm, though it's already becoming a little long in the tooth.
My desktop situation includes a dual monitor setup with a modest Acer monitor. I also use a Logitech vertical mouse (who can use these ThinkPad trackpads) and a Havit keyboard (my first mechanical keyboard; I love it but my wife hates it!). I'm a recent convert from wired headphones; I have Anker Soundcore Liberty Air wireless earbuds for personal use and have taken to the Sennheiser HD 450BT headphones for work.
Whenever I have a second to myself, I'm probably gaming on my Nintendo Switch 2, Steam Deck, or Xbox Series S. I also still have a bunch of classic consoles lying around as well.

item.content:encoded:
The San Diego Padres are expected to make major roster changes this winter.
San Diego has a ton of potential free agents this winter, and the reality is, they can't keep all of them. To reach their ultimate goal, it may be best to not retain a majority of them.
Sometimes, change is necessary, especially for a team that hasn't been able to get over the hump. The Padres' ultimate goal is to win a World Series, and while no single player can get them there alone, pending free agent Tarik Skubal could be a key missing piece.
ESPN MLB insider Kiley McDaniel noted that some experts named the Padres as "sleepers" to land Skubal.
"The Los Angeles Angels, Chicago White Sox and San Diego Padres were mentioned in this category; the Angels and Padres have new ownership, and the White Sox have a new owner in waiting," McDaniel wrote. "In most high-end free agent bidding processes, there's at least one surprising or mystery team. After circling back with some sources after the projections were in, the Padres seemed to be the consensus pick for the most serious bidder in this group."
McDaniel named the New York Mets, Detroit Tigers and the Los Angeles Dodgers as the true contenders to land the two-time Cy Young winner.
Skubal is projected to sign a contract worth north of $400 million this winter. A contract of that magnitude would make him by far the highest-paid pitcher in MLB history.
Can the Padres Afford to Sign Tarik Skubal?
It's unclear if the Padres have the financial capacity to afford Skubal. A lot of that depends on how agrressive their new owners want to be.
Jose E. Feliciano and Kwanza Jones paid $3.9 billion to purchase the Padres. They have plans to win, but also inherited a high payroll.
While they want to be competitive, they will be more methodical in their approach.
If the Padres feel it is safe enough to go after Skubal, they won't think twice.
The 29-year-old ace is arguably the league's best pitcher. In 2026, Skubal went 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA, 186 strikeouts and a 0.96 WHIP in 26 starts and 158.2 innings with the Detroit Tigers and Los Angeles Dodgers. The last two years, he's won two Cy Young awards in the American League.
Skubal is the kind of pitcher that could single-handedly win a team a playoff series.
The starting rotation is also by far the Padres' biggest need. But whether they can afford Skubal — while also filling out a rotation expected to lose most of its pitchers — remains to be seen.

Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.title: [WSLS] Chase DeLauter and José Ramírez lead the Guardians to a 7-3 win over the Rays in Game 1 of the ALCS
item.dc:creator: Rob Maaddi; Associated Press
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – The Cleveland Guardians used small ball, the longball and played solid all-around baseball to keep winning in the postseason. Nathaniel Lowe snapped an eighth-inning tie with a two-run single after Chase DeLauter and Patrick Bailey homered off Drew Rasmussen, and the Guardians rallied past the Tampa Bay Rays 7-3 in Game 1 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night. item.content:encoded:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – The Cleveland Guardians used small ball, the longball and played solid all-around baseball to keep winning in the postseason.
Nathaniel Lowe snapped an eighth-inning tie with a two-run single after Chase DeLauter and Patrick Bailey homered off Drew Rasmussen, and the Guardians rallied past the Tampa Bay Rays 7-3 in Game 1 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night.
Recommended Videos
After losing the first two games at home to the Chicago White Sox in their AL Division Series, Cleveland has won four straight in the postseason for the first time since winning their first six playoff games in 2016 on the way to a World Series berth.
“It feels good to see some balls fall, to see some guys get on the barrel, to see some guys have some great at-bats, because the first two games of the White Sox series, we got beat. We did,” Lowe said. “We had to go get our backs against the wall and do something crazy, and this group did. It’s nice to feel some momentum coming here and to take Game 1.”
Jose Ramírez had three hits and DeLauter was a triple shy of the cycle as the Guardians banged out 14 hits against a Tampa Bay staff that allowed just 12 in its entire Division Series against the New York Yankees.
Junior Caminero and Jonny DeLuca had RBI singles in the first and Cedric Mullins hit a solo homer for the Rays, who never trailed in their three-game sweep of the Yankees.
“It’s been a while since we lost, so I think that’s a good thing, and I know the guys will come back and respond tomorrow,” Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said.
Game 2 is Tuesday night at Tropicana Field. Rookie left-hander Parker Messick starts for Cleveland, and right-hander Freddy Peralta takes the mound for the Rays.
Five relievers combined for five innings of one-run, two-hit ball for the Guardians, who became only the 11th team to overcome an 0-2 deficit in a best-of-five playoff series with a victory over the White Sox on Saturday night.
Hunter Gaddis worked a scoreless seventh for the win. Cade Smith, who pitched in all five games against Chicago, tossed a perfect ninth.
“Obviously we came off an emotional series, had a quick turnaround. But these guys come ready to play every day. Couldn’t be more proud of them,” Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said. “We got punched early. And our pitching staff, credit to them, for stopping it and keeping us in the game as long as they did. And the offense came alive.”
Rasmussen took a 2-0 lead into the sixth before DeLauter led off with an opposite-field homer to left-center. Bailey started the seventh with a towering shot to center that went a projected 436 feet, ending Rasmussen’s night.
Rasmussen carried a no-hitter into the eighth in Game 1 of the ALDS against the Yankees.
Ramírez opened the eighth with an infield single off losing pitcher Tyler Wells, and DeLauter ripped a double to right. After Wells retired Jo Adell on a grounder to second, Ian Seymour entered. Lowe lined an 0-2 pitch up the middle to drive in two, giving Cleveland a 4-2 lead.
Lowe made his major league debut with Tampa Bay in 2019 and won a World Series with Texas in 2023.
“I love coming back here, I really do,” Lowe said. “It’s nice to see some familiar faces on the other side.”
Mullins connected off Erik Sabrowski for a solo shot in the bottom half.
Ramírez, whose two-run homer lifted Cleveland to a 2-0 win in Game 5 against Chicago, provided an insurance run with an RBI single in the ninth off Cole Sulser.
Ramírez then helped the Guardians get two more by breaking for third with two outs and two strikes on Adell. Caminero ran to cover the bag and was out of position when Adell hit a sharp grounder toward third. The ball rolled into left field for a two-run double.
A crowd of 35,361 fans waved yellow rally towels and rang cowbells at the Trop as Tampa Bay made its third ALCS appearance in the franchise's 29-season history.
They were fired up when the 98-win Rays jumped ahead 2-0 in the first and Rasmussen battled to keep it there until the sixth.
Coming off that dominant performance against the Yankees, Rasmussen went six-plus tough innings. The two-time All-Star right-hander, who was four outs from a no-hitter in a 1-0 victory against New York, allowed a hit to the second batter he faced and eight total, striking out seven.
Guardians starter Foster Griffin gave up two runs and five hits in four innings.
Glove work
The Rays helped Rasmussen with outstanding defense.
Nick Fortes threw out Ramírez trying to steal second in the first. Caminero made an excellent play to retire Adell on a hard bouncer to third. Caminero short-hopped the ball with his backhand and fired a strong throw to first.
The Guardians had a runner on first with one out in the third when second baseman Ben Williamson robbed DeLauter of a hit that prevented a first-and-third jam. Williamson, who wasn’t on the ALDS roster, made a diving grab on DeLauter’s sharp grounder, got up and threw him out.
Stranded runners
Rays slick-fielding shortstop Taylor Walls was 0 for 3 and left six runners on base. He struck out with the bases loaded to end the first, lined out with a runner on in the fourth and grounded out with runners on first and second to end the sixth.
Up next
Messick took the loss in Game 1 of the AL Division Series, allowing two runs over 4 1/3 innings. He threw 2 1/3 innings in relief during a Game 4 victory, giving up two runs. Messick had 11 strikeouts in the two appearances. He was 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA in the regular season.
Peralta allowed one run and three hits over 4 2/3 innings in Game 2 of the Division Series vs. the Yankees. He was 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 starts after joining Tampa Bay at the trade deadline. Peralta was 5-9 with a 4.99 ERA for the Mets this season.
___

item.content:encoded:
Brewers bullpen makes MLB playoff history by silencing Dodgers in NLCS Game 2 originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The reigning World Series champions aren't totally on the brink just yet, but the Brewers have the Dodgers playing for their season as the NLCS shifts to Los Angeles.
The Brewers took the first two games of the series the only way they know how: manufacturing runs and slamming the door with a stellar bullpen.
Milwaukee's bullpen is no stranger to success, but its performance in Game 2 took dominance to a new level as the Brewers closed out a come-from-behind 7-4 victory.
Here's a look at how the Brewers' arsenal of relievers made MLB history on Monday night.
Brewers bullpen makes MLB history
The Brewers out-hit the Dodgers 12-3 on Monday, but it was a 4-3 game in favor of the Dodgers halfway through the fifth inning. An electrifying performance by the bullpen is a major reason why Milwaukee was able to climb back in front for a third and final time.
The unit tossed five perfect innings in the win, facing 15 batters and getting 15 outs. That made the Brewers the first team in playoff history to get five perfect innings out of a bullpen.
The bullpen did surrender a run, as an inherited runner scored on a sacrifice fly off Dustin May in the fifth inning, but May got three outs without allowing a baserunner of his own while JoJo Romero, Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby slammed the door with perfect outings of their own.
Here's the breakdown:
- Dustin May: 1.0 IP, 0 H, 0 ER, 1 K
- JoJo Romero: 1.0 IP, 0 H, 0 ER, 2 K
- Abner Uribe: 1.1 IP, 0 H, 0 ER, 2 K
- Aaron Ashby: 1.2 IP, 0 H, 0 ER, 2 K
May and Romero each covered an inning, while Uribe and Ashby combined to get the final nine outs against the Dodgers. Not only did Pat Murphy get perfection out of his bullpen, but he was able to preserve closer Trevor Megill, who will enter Game 3 off back-to-back rest days.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have fallen 0-1 in the National League Champion Series to the Milwaukee Brewers. While the Dodgers looked like they had the edge over the now-World Series favorites, the nine runners left on base and three GIDP sealed their fate.
As they continue to trek towards a three-peat, it's hard not to reflect on the past, when the Dodgers dynasty began. Only five players from the Dodgers 2020 World Series remain; Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Will Smith, and Blake Treinen.
Their World Series MVP Corey Seager, left in 2022 to sign with the Texas Rangers, where he has been ever since. Adding another World Series MVP to his trophy shelf, but falling to injury nearly every year after.
Now that the Rangers season is done, they're gearing up to explore trade options, and Seager may be one of them. However, Seager and the Rangers may have gotten a bit of a reality check after Bleacher Report's ranking of MLB's top 25 trade chips.
Did the Dodgers Win the Corey Seager Debate? SS Ranked 15th After Recent Elbow Surgery And $157.5 Million Left on Contract
In a recent article by MLB analyst Joel Reuter of Bleacher Report, he ranks the top 25 MLB trade chips of the 2026-2027 offseason. Corey Seager, a two-time World Series MVP, five-time All-Star, three-time Silver Slugger, and 2016 Rookie of the Year is ranked 15th-out-of-25.
While that number may seem shocking, Seager is 32 years old and underwent another surgey on his elbow. During Seager's time with the Rangers, he's missed over 250 games due to injury.
"A $31.5 million annual salary for the next five seasons, coupled with his lengthy injury history, won't make it easy for the Rangers to move Seager," Reuter wrote. "That said, he remains a star-level performer when healthy, and a thin shortstop class in free agency will shift focus to the trade market. For a team not willing to pay the steep price to acquire someone like Zach Neto or Otto Lopez, absorbing Seager's salary at a lower acquisition cost is a potential alternative."
While it's important to note that Reuter doesn't say that it will be impossible to trade Seager, he comes with a huge cost. A dent in the payroll and a risk for time spent on the injured list.
With the talks of Seager being traded, it resurfaces the debate of whether or not the Dodgers made a mistake by not re-signing Seager to the contract he deserved at the time. He did bring them a World Series in 2020.
In 2018, Seager underwent a midseason Tommy John surgery, leaving the Dodgers to rent Manny Machado for the remainder of the season. 2021, Seager fractured his right hand, missing 65 games which prompted the Trea Turner, Max Scherzer trade.
In his second season with the Rangers, Seager made history by being the first player to win multiple World Series MVPs with different franchises.
The Rangers 2023 World Series win left the Dodgers with a bitter taste in their mouth. And since then, the Rangers have yet to find their way back into the playoffs, whereas the Dodgers are en route to their third World Series in as many years.
Seager's departure allowed the Dodgers to take on the contracts of Shohei Ohtani, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Freddie Freeman. Two of which were World Series MVPs, and the other making history as the first player to record 10 Ks while hitting three home runs.
Teams Potentially Interested in Corey Seager
While Seager's contract isn't an easy one to swallow, the shortstop is still one of the most consistent players on both defense and offense in the league.
Last offseason, the Boston Red Sox were interested in Seager, but the Rangers weren't willing to move him.
Joel Sherman of MLB Network, recently stated that the Atlanta Braves checked in on Seager last offseason.
"A lot of teams checked in on Seager last offseason," Sherman said. "I believe Atlanta was one of those teams. I wouldn't be surprised if they did it again."
The Braves wouldn't be a surprising destination for Seager. Atlanta is need for a change after their early departure in the postseason this year. Rumors of trading Ronald Acuña Jr. and Ozzie Albies have begun swirling.
If the Braves were to trade Acuña and Albies, that would free up around $24 million a year, which nearly covers Seagers contract, and they don't have to worry about another big extension.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Los Angeles Dodgers Get Intriguing Corey Seager Trade News After NLCS Loss appeared first on HEAVY.

item.title: [Bettors Insider] Shohei Ohtani, Jonathan Aranda, Junior Caminero Props: 3 MLB Batter Bets to Back Today | Bettors Insider
item.dc:creator: Earnest Horn

item.content:encoded:
October baseball is a different animal for prop bettors — smaller sample, bigger stakes, and lineups built around whoever’s been carrying their team through the first two rounds. Monday’s slate gives us two of those players squarely in the spotlight: Shohei Ohtani trying to find his timing again in Milwaukee, and a pair of Tampa Bay bats that have already authored the signature moments of their ALDS sweep heading into Game 1 of the ALCS against Cleveland.
None of these three lines are “free money,” and we’re not pretending otherwise. But each one is backed by a real statistical case, and one of them is a legitimate longshot worth a small piece of your bankroll. Here’s the breakdown.
Shohei Ohtani Hits Over 0.5 (-115) vs. Logan Henderson
Ohtani’s .275/.377/.512 slash line with 30 home runs, 144 hits, and 268 total bases over 135 games this season is the baseline case for betting him to reach base in literally any game he plays. A .377 on-base percentage means Ohtani is getting on base better than one out of every three plate appearances even before you isolate hits specifically, and his contact skills remain elite even in a year where he split time managing a knee issue.
The matchup context matters here too. Henderson is a rookie-caliber arm who hasn’t faced a lineup with this level of postseason pressure attached to it, and the Dodgers as a group have shown they can grind out at-bats against less experienced starters. At just 0.5 hits, this line is asking Ohtani for a single knock in what will likely be 4-5 plate appearances. Even accounting for recent cold stretches, betting against Shohei Ohtani recording one hit in a full game remains one of the tougher outs in the sport to actually complete.
Jonathan Aranda Hits Over 0.5 vs. Franco Griffin
If you watched any of the Rays-Yankees ALDS, you already know the Aranda story. His third-inning solo shot off Gerrit Cole in Game 1 — a 417-foot blast to right-center — was the only run of a 1-0 series-opening win, and it set the tone for a clean three-game sweep. Across that series, Aranda hit .333/.385/.583 for a .968 OPS, numbers that dwarf his already-solid .274/.358/.434 season line.
That’s the core of the case: Aranda is seeing the ball well right now, has shown he can do damage against a well above-average Yankees pitching staff, and now draws a left-handed starter in Griffin to open the ALCS. First baseman with sticky contact skills facing a lefty he hasn’t built extensive familiarity with is a profile that tends to produce base hits, not shutouts. At 0.5 hits, the number is simply asking for one knock from a hitter who’s been getting multiple most nights since the calendar flipped to October.
Junior Caminero Home Run Over 0.5 (+525 BetRivers)
This is the one we’re framing honestly: a value shot, not a lock. Caminero is coming off a 42-homer season — his second straight 40-bomb campaign — and projection models still put him around a 0.24 expected home run probability for any single game, which sits below what the plus-money price implies you need for a coin-flip bet. In other words, this isn’t the kind of prop where the math says “take the over all day.” It’s a power bet on a player who has legitimate 40-plus-homer pop and a juicy price if he connects.
Where it gets more interesting is the matchup and the moment. Caminero is drawing another lefty in Griffin tonight, and left-on-right power threats like Caminero have shown they can turn a mistake into a souvenir in a hurry — he’s also shown an .817 OPS against the Yankees in this postseason run specifically, proof the bat is playing up on the biggest stage, not shrinking from it. At +525, you’re not betting that Caminero goes deep most nights. You’re betting that on a night where ESPN’s own expert panel has him tabbed as a leading ALCS MVP pick, the long ball is live enough to make the number worth a small stake.
Today’s Edge
Two contact-driven hits bets and one true power longshot — that’s the balance we’re carrying into Monday’s games. Always confirm the latest line movement with your sportsbook before locking anything in, since postseason numbers can shift quickly as lineups are finalized.
- Shohei Ohtani OVER 0.5 Hits (-115)
- Jonathan Aranda OVER 0.5 Hits
- Junior Caminero OVER 0.5 Home Runs (+525 BetRivers)
The hits props lean on two hitters who have been nearly impossible to keep off base in October, while the Caminero shot gives this card real upside if the Rays’ slugger connects early in the ALCS. If you’re shopping for better plus-money odds on power props like that one, it’s worth comparing a few books before locking in your DraftKings Promo Code or another book’s current offer.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Brewers get just enough off Tarik Skubal, draw first blood in NLCS Game 1 win
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee

item.content:encoded:
First and foremost, the Dodgers wanted Tarik Skubal on their team. When they pursued him at the trade deadline, they saw him as the rare player who could improve their odds of winning a third straight World Series.
It didn't hurt that by acquiring him they prevented other postseason contenders, including the Milwaukee Brewers, from landing the two-time Cy Young Award winner. The Dodgers guaranteed that they wouldn't have to face him in October.
"I'm sure it's in the back of your head, the teams that are interested," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Sunday before the Dodgers' 2-1 loss to the Brewers in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series. "Certainly not a driver, but not nothing either. As far as how happy I am, I am very happy it's Skubal versus Miz and not Miz and Skubal [for the Brewers] in the next two."
Read more: Dodgers struggle against Milwaukee Brewers pitching in NLCS Game 1 loss
That sentiment rang even truer when the Dodgers dropped Game 1 at American Family Field, despite forcing "Miz" — Jacob Misiorowski, the NL Cy Young favorite — out of the game in just 4⅓ innings, and despite having Skubal, who lasted five innings but gave up two runs in a fine effort, on their side.
In a role reversal, the Dodgers, who scored almost exclusively via the home run in the first round, pulled ahead with a pesky approach at the plate.
Designated hitter Shohei Ohtani opened the second inning with a four-pitch walk. Then Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit opposite-field singles to move Ohtani around the bases and give the Dodgers a 1-0 lead.
Taking a similar "grind him out" approach to the one they deployed against Atlanta Braves ace Chris Sale in Game 3 of the division series, the Dodgers forced Misiorowski to throw 35 pitches in the inning — 10 alone to Kyle Tucker, who worked a walk.
By the third inning, Misiorowski's fastball velocity, which touched 104 mph, had dropped to double digits. And though the Dodgers didn't score again against him, they continued to rack up his pitch count. By the time he exited with one out in the fifth, it was at 94.
The Brewers, known for their peskiness, instead tied the game with one swing against Skubal. In the bottom of the fourth inning, Brice Turang got the barrel of his bat to an inside sinker and lifted it over the fence in left-center, into the Brewers bullpen.
If Turang, who went two for 16 in the NLDS, is heating up at the plate, that could be bad news for the Dodgers.
Though the Brewers have players who can hit home runs, they pulled ahead the next inning with a sequence more closely aligned with their identity.
Skubal walked Garrett Mitchell on five pitches. Brewers rookie Cooper Pratt moved him into scoring position with a sacrifice bunt. And then Luis Lara sent a ground-ball single through the middle of the infield to drive in the go-ahead run.
Skubal battled traffic to get out of the inning without giving up another run. But in such a tight game, that marked the end of his start.
The American Family Field atmosphere added an extra charge to the close contest. The home crowd was perhaps its loudest (until an ear-splitting cheer at the final out) when it took issue with a balk call against Misiorowski. It looked as if he had picked off Hernández to end the fourth inning, but Hernández instead was awarded second base.
That play still was seared into their collective memory when Dodgers left-hander Alex Vesia picked off Jack Bauers at first base. Brewers fans shouted "balk!" over and over.
The bullpens battled to a scoreless draw, the Dodgers' last stand falling flat after Tucker and pinch-hitting rookie Josue De Paula drew a pair of two-out walks against Trevor Megill. But the Brewers closer got Mookie Betts to fly out and end it, as the edge the Brewers gained against Skubal held.
The road doesn't get much easier for the Dodgers in Game 2, when they'll face right-hander Logan Henderson, who held them to one run in seven innings when the Brewers came to Los Angeles in August. But imagine if instead the Brewers had outbid the Dodgers and they had to go through Skubal first.
"It would look really different," manager Dave Roberts said Saturday. "What those guys do — they had the best record in baseball. Certainly when you're talking about a seven-game series, to see Tarik on the other side … the series would look a lot different."
This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times.

item.title: [MLB.com] LIVE: Dodgers-Brewers NLCS Game 1 on FOX/FOX One

item.content:encoded:
The National League’s two best teams in the regular season are the last two standing at the end. The 103-win Brewers against the 100-win Dodgers.
Who’s ready for a rematch of last year’s NLCS?
“Coming into the postseason, you had a feeling you were going to have to go through L.A.,” said Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich. “They’re back-to-back champs, and they’re a great team. We have a lot of respect for those guys.
“At the same time, we feel like we can play with anybody when we play our game. When we play our brand of baseball, when we play clean and execute, we’re a really hard team to beat. We’re going to go in there and grind.”
For the Dodgers, this year’s NLCS is a chance to continue a bid for a third consecutive World Series title.
For the Brewers, it’s a chance at redemption. They have been to the League Championship Series five times in their franchise history, and this is the third in a row that pits them against the Dodgers. They lost a seven-game thriller in 2018, then got swept in four games last year, when Brewers hitters were shut down by the Dodgers’ superstar starting pitchers.
Will this year be different?
"In this sport, you can't carry previous postseasons into this postseason. Everything is a new chapter," said Dodgers utility man Kiké Hernández. "Every time you take the field in October, you get an opportunity to rewrite your story."
When is the game and how can I watch it?
Game 1 is underway at American Family Field and airing nationally on FOX, FOX Deportes and FOX One.
All series are available in the US on MLB.TV with authentication to a participating Pay TV provider. Games also are available live internationally, although not in Canada. Sportsnet is MLB's exclusive English language broadcaster in Canada for every Postseason game, while TVA Sports will be covering the entire AL Postseason and the World Series in French and Broadcaster RDS will cover the entire NL Postseason in French.
Skubal showed exactly why the Dodgers swung big to acquire him from the Tigers ahead of the Trade Deadline in his NLDS Game 1 start, when he struck out seven across six innings of one-run ball against the Braves. Now, he will take the hill as L.A. begins the next stage of its title defense.
Misiorowski’s first pitch of NLDS Game 1 was 104.8 mph, the fastest postseason pitch in the pitch tracking era, which dates back to 2008. But the Padres made him work, fouling off an incredible 30 pitches in the first four innings to knock Misiorowski out of the game by the fifth at 88 pitches. He was in the bullpen for Game 4 in San Diego, and even warmed up in the ninth, but was not needed, meaning he will be rested and ready for the Dodgers. In three career appearances against L.A. – two starts in the regular season and one relief outing in last year’s NLCS – Misiorowski has a 1.59 ERA and 27 strikeouts vs. three walks in 17 innings.
What are the starting lineups?
Dodgers: The Dodgers have dropped Shohei Ohtani in the lineup as his struggles from the end of the regular season have bled into the beginning of the postseason. Misiorowski has been tough on L.A. in the past, so manager Dave Roberts shuffled his lineup to optimize the matchups.
Brewers: The Brewers don’t hit many home runs, but they can hit home runs, and they can score in a lot of ways. During the regular season, they were second in the Majors in runs scored by hitting for average (.258, first in MLB), getting on base (.341, first), stealing bases (152, fifth), bunting (32 bunt hits, second) and generally refusing to swing the bat until they wanted to (lowest swing percentage in MLB and lowest chase percentage). Against the Padres in the NLDS, they came from behind in two of the three victories. Here’s how they're lining up against Skubal in Game 1.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Dodgers: Edwin Díaz saved the final two games of the NLDS and is firmly back in the closer's mix, with Tanner Scott also an option to lock down save situations. The Dodgers added a 13th pitcher while setting their 26-man roster for the NL Championship Series. Left-hander Justin Wrobleski joined the bullpen, while speed option Hyeseong Kim was left off the roster.
Brewers: Brewers relievers covered 19 innings in four games against the Padres with a 0.47 ERA and a .169 opposing average, led by the late-inning trio of left-hander Aaron Ashby, right-hander Abner Uribe and righty closer Trevor Megill. Uribe pitched in all four games, and Ashby and Megill in three, so a couple days off will be appreciated.
Any injuries of note?
Dodgers: Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) and Freeman (right knee) are managing lingering injuries. Rojas exited Game 3 with lower back pain, and while his availability for the beginning of the NLCS was uncertain, he is on the roster. World Series hero Will Klein (right elbow discomfort) has faced hitters, but he has not pitched in a game since July 31 and is viewed as more of a depth option. Blake Treinen (right shoulder inflammation) is unlikely to pitch this postseason.
Brewers: None.
Who is hot and who is not?
Dodgers: Freeman (.267, two homers), Muncy (.250, three homers) and Tucker (.333) have been among L.A.'s most consistent hitters this postseason. Smith (.063) and Ohtani (.154) are looking to shake off slow starts at the plate.
Brewers: Contreras led the Majors with 24 RBIs in September, had a .933 OPS from Sept. 9 through the end of the regular season, and then stayed hot in the NLDS, slashing .375/.444/.750 with a pair of home runs against the Padres. The Brewers would love to get Turang going again. His .361 average and .475 on-base percentage led the Majors in September and his 1.077 OPS was in the top 10, but he went 2-for-16 in the NLDS.
Anything else fans might want to know?
- Besides the three previous NLCS matchups, the Brewers and Dodgers also met in the 2020 NL Wild Card Series. The Dodgers swept in two games.
- This is the seventh time that the NLCS has pitted the same teams in back-to-back seasons. That also happened in 2020-21 (Braves and Dodgers), 2016-17 (Cubs and Dodgers), 2008-09 (Dodgers and Phillies), 2004-05 (Astros and Cardinals), 1991-92 (Braves and Pirates) and 1977-78 (Dodgers and Phillies).
- The Brewers are one of five teams -- along with the Mariners, Padres, Rays and Rockies -- that has never won the World Series.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] “Got Exposed This Year”: Blue Jays Vet Explains How Alejandro Kirk’s Absence Affected Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Singh
item.description: Toronto Blue Jays veteran Kevin Pillar believes Alejandro Kirk's absence from the lineup contributed to Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s disappointing 2026 season, arguing that the first baseman struggled without reliable protection behind him.
