item.content:encoded:
Blue Jays made right Bo Bichette decision after latest Mets report on infielder originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
When the Toronto Blue Jays decided to move on from star shortstop Bo Bichette, it was met with some skepticism.
It was obvious why the Blue Jays did so, at least in the simple sense that they didn't want to pay him as much as he was asking. Bichette ended up signing a somewhat ridiculous contract with the New York Mets, earning $126 million over three years.
He also got two player options after each season, making it a deal that would have been tough to pass up.
As for whether Toronto made the right decision in moving on from Bichette, that's not something we can determine yet, though early returns suggest it did what it was supposed to do.
According to a report, if Bichette opts out of his deal with the Mets, he's very unlikely to get more than his $42 million AAV.
That alone shows that the Blue Jays might have made the right decision if they weren't willing to give him a contract in that same ballpark.
"If he opts out, Bichette will find it impossible to eclipse his current deal's $42 million average annual value. Even if he does wish to opt out for non-financial reasons, Bichette can still do so a year from now at age 29, presumably off a better platform season. For all those reasons, he is likely to stay. Bichette's decision is due five days after the World Series ends," Anthony DiComo wrote.
It's always tough to get a feel for contracts like this for a guy who has led the American League twice in hits and has frankly been one of the better offensive infielders in baseball for much of his career.
However, Bichette has other problems as a player, which were evident in New York this past season.

item.content:encoded:
Oct 8, 2026, 11:35 AM ET
New York Yankees impending free-agent first baseman/designated hitter Paul Goldschmidt has expressed a desire to keep playing at age 39 in 2027, according to Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News. It is unclear if the Yankees will make an effort to re-sign the former MVP and seven-time All-Star in the offseason. Goldy had a nice bounce-back campaign in 2026 in his 16th year in the big leagues after he hit just 10 homers and drove in 45 runs in 146 games in 2025 in his first year in pinstripes. In 105 regular-season games across 380 plate appearances this year, Goldschmidt hit .252/.313/.452 with a .765 OPS, 18 home runs, 52 RBI, and 44 runs scored for the Yankees. He went hitless in eight plate appearances with two walks and a run scored in four postseason games for New York this year. Goldschmidt is obviously no longer in his prime and is no longer an everyday player, but he should still attract interest across the league for his ability to hit lefties. In 183 plate appearances against southpaws in 2026, he hit .299 (47-for-157) with 11 of his 18 home runs and 24 RBI.--Keith Hernandez
Source: New York Daily News - Gary Phillips
More Recent News
Oct 8, 2026, 11:28 AM ET
Tampa Bay Rays closer Bryan Baker shut the door in his team's 4-3 win over the New York Yankees in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with two strikeouts. Baker was a key part of Tampa Bay's three-game sweep of New York, logging saves in all three games while allowing just one baserunner to reach. The 31-year-old emerged as one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, recording a 1.44 ERA and 0.91 WHIP with 63 strikeouts and 41 saves across 62 1/3 innings (65 games). Heading into the American League Championship Series, Baker's dominance at the end of games gives Tampa Bay a significant advantage if it can get an early lead on its opponents.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Jakob Marsee Having UCL Repair With Internal Brace


Keith Hernandez




Oct 8, 2026, 11:24 AM ET
Miami Marlins outfielder Jakob Marsee (elbow) will get a UCL repair with an internal brace of his left elbow on Monday, according to Christina De Nicola of MLB.com. The estimated return-to-play timeline for Marsee is around six months. Marsee battled through elbow issues down the stretch in 2026 in his first full season in the majors with Miami. In his first taste of the big leagues in 2025, Marsee hit .292 (61-for-209) with five home runs, 33 RBI, 14 stolen bases, and 28 runs scored in 55 games and 234 plate appearances. In 155 games and 616 plate appearances this year, Marsee slashed .231/.348/.359 with a .706 OPS, 11 home runs, 41 RBI, 23 stolen bases, and 83 runs scored for the Fish. The 25-year-old former sixth-round pick by the San Diego Padres in 2022 from Central Michigan University has a very intriguing power/speed profile as an outfielder in all fantasy leagues, but his availability for Opening Day in 2027 could be in question, depending on how he fares during his rehab after going under the knife early next week.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Christina De Nicola
Oct 8, 2026, 11:21 AM ET
Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Garrett Mitchell had a big game in his team's 3-1, series-clinching win over the San Diego Padres in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday. At the plate, Mitchell went two-for-four with a triple, an RBI, and a run scored. In the field, Mitchell robbed Padres third baseman Manny Machado of what would have been a game-tying two-run home run in the eighth inning. The 28-year-old Mitchell was finally able to stay mostly healthy in 2026, hitting .262/.354/.416 with 11 home runs, 65 RBI, 74 runs scored, and 14 stolen bases across 531 plate appearances in the regular season. He was productive in the NLDS as well, logging four hits, three runs scored, an RBI, and a stolen base across 15 at-bats.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Hagen Smith Opening Game 4 of ALDS on Thursday


Keith Hernandez




Oct 8, 2026, 11:15 AM ET
Chicago White Sox rookie left-hander Hagen Smith will serve as the opener in Game 4 of the American League Division Series on Thursday at home against the division-rival Cleveland Guardians, according to Scott Merkin of MLB.com. The 23-year-old former fifth overall pick in 2024 from the University of Arkansas made 18 appearances (only one start) in his major-league debut during the 2026 regular season, posting a nice 1.29 ERA (2.35 FIP) and 0.96 WHIP with 41 strikeouts and 16 walks in 28 innings pitched. The talented young southpaw has already thrown 6 1/3 innings in his first experience in the playoffs, too, allowing just one earned run on three hits while walking five and striking out six. He started Game 1 of the ALDS against Cleveland and threw 2 2/3 shutout innings with three walks and four strikeouts in the team's 3-0 victory before allowing a run with two walks and a strikeout in two-thirds of an inning in Wednesday's Game 3 loss. Smith will probably have a short leash as the White Sox try to close out the best-of-five series, with right-hander Erick Fedde potentially piggybacking Smith in Chicago. In three relief appearances against the Guardians during the regular season, Smith allowed two earned runs with six walks and eight strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings pitched.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Scott Merkin
Victor Mesa Jr. Homers in ALDS-Clinching Win


Will Brady




Oct 8, 2026, 11:14 AM ET
Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Victor Mesa Jr. was one of the stars of his team's 4-3 win in Game 3 of the American League Division Series over the New York Yankees, hitting a two-run home run off Yankees left-hander Max Fried. Mesa Jr.'s home run was his only hit of the night, but it gave the Rays a 4-2 lead in the sixth inning that they would ultimately never give back. Across 262 plate appearances in the regular season, Mesa Jr. hit .260/.327/.498 with 14 home runs, 34 RBI, 37 runs scored, and nine stolen bases. After starting the year in the minors, the 25-year-old has emerged as an everyday corner outfielder for Tampa Bay and provides another dynamic power/speed bat for the Rays. If Mesa Jr. can get hot, he could help power a deep postseason run.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 10:01 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz picked up his second save in as many nights on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with a strikeout in his team's 4-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series. Diaz missed most of the 2026 regular season due to elbow and neck injuries. However, he's been dominant since returning from the injured list in mid-September. Diaz allowed just two baserunners while notching nine strikeouts in his final five innings pitched of the regular season, and he's now logged low-stress saves in each of his first two appearances of the playoffs. With Diaz rounding into form, Los Angeles' bullpen looks like a major strength heading into the National League Championship Series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:52 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians left-hander Foster Griffin was dominant in a bulk relief appearance in his team's 9-3 win over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Griffin followed Cleveland opener Daniel Espino and allowed two hits and one earned run while striking out seven across 2 2/3 innings of work. The 31-year-old was used exclusively as a starting pitcher during the regular season, posting a 15-6 record with a 3.60 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, and 158 strikeouts across 172 2/3 innings (31 starts) split between the Guardians and the Washington Nationals. However, Griffin struggled mightily late in the year, pitching to a 5.05 ERA in the second half and a 6.87 ERA across 18 1/3 innings in September. If Griffin can rediscover his early-season form in a bullpen role, he could help Cleveland mount a comeback in the ALDS.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:43 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians outfielder Jo Adell had a big night in his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, going 2-for-4 with a walk and three RBI. With the game tied 1-1 in the third inning, Adell put the Guardians ahead for good with a three-run triple off of White Sox left-hander Hagen Smith. Across 660 regular-season plate appearances split between the Guardians and the Los Angeles Angels, Adell hit .240/.298/.401 with 23 home runs, 94 RBI, 70 runs scored, and five stolen bases. He was better with Cleveland than he was with Los Angeles, posting a .740 OPS across 204 trips to the plate after the Guardians acquired him at the trade deadline. Adell has notched a couple of key hits for Cleveland in the ALDS and now has four RBI across the first three games of the series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:32 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages had the key hit in his team's 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday, logging a go-ahead two-run single off Braves right-hander Robert Suarez in the seventh inning. Pages finished the game with two hits and two RBI in three at-bats. The 25-year-old was a critical piece of the Dodgers lineup during the regular season, hitting .274 with 23 home runs, 85 RBI, 75 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases. However, Pages struggled mightily during the Dodgers' run to the 2025 World Series, notching just four hits in 55 postseason plate appearances. After his big night on Wednesday, Pages has already logged four hits in just 15 plate appearances in the 2026 playoffs.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:19 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians right-hander Cade Smith was lights out to secure his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Smith entered the game in the eighth inning and recorded the final six outs, logging five strikeouts without allowing a single baserunner. The 27-year-old was one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, pitching to a 1.95 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 107 strikeouts and 41 saves across 74 innings (69 games). Smith has been dominant so far in the Division Series as well, as he's yet to allow a hit or a walk in his four innings of work. If Cleveland is going to mount a comeback in the series, it will likely need Smith to continue his dominance.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:11 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez was one of the stars of his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series. In five plate appearances, Ramirez recorded a double, a triple, a walk, two RBI, two runs scored, and a stolen base. With Cleveland leading 5-3 in the 8th inning, it was Ramirez's two-run triple that sealed the win for the Guardians and kept the series alive to see Game 4. The 34-year-old battled through injuries and underperformance in 2026, hitting .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs, 53 RBI, 71 runs scored, and 37 stolen bases across 544 plate appearances. Ramirez also got off to a slow start in the postseason, going hitless in his first eight trips to the plate against the White Sox. If Cleveland is going to rally all the way back from two games down in the ALDS, it will need Ramirez to stay hot in Games 4 and 5.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Robert Gasser Starting Game 4 of NLDS Against Padres


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:08 PM ET
Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser will start for the Brewers in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the San Diego Padres, according to Brewers reporter Sophia Minnaert. It will be Gasser's first career postseason start after throwing 2 2/3 innings of relief in the playoffs for the Brew Crew last year. The 27-year-old southpaw went 5-5 on the season with a 3.87 ERA (4.24 FIP) and 1.19 WHIP with a career-high 103 strikeouts and 35 walks in 109 1/3 innings across 21 appearances (20 starts). The problem for Gasser is that he has not made a start in almost two weeks, so he could be a bit rusty. Manager Pat Murphy will surely have a short hook on the young left-hander as the Brewers look to close the best-of-five series out in San Diego. Gasser was outstanding down the stretch in 2026, allowing two earned runs or fewer in each of his last six starts, walking 12 and striking out 31 in 32 1/3 innings during that span. He did not face the Padres at all during the regular season, which could give him a bit of an advantage.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Sophia Minnaert
Mason Miller Back From the Paternity List for Game 4


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:03 PM ET
The San Diego Padres announced on Wednesday that they returned right-handed closer Mason Miller from the paternity list, taking the place on the National League Division Series roster of left-handed reliever Wandy Peralta. Miller blew a two-inning save in Game 2 of the series in Milwaukee against the Brewers and was then unavailable for the win in Game 3 at Petco Park on Tuesday night. It is great news for the Padres, who did not have left-handed high-leverage reliever Adrian Morejon on Tuesday due to a left-shoulder issue. The Padres had to go to Game 1 starter, right-hander Michael King, for the two-inning save with both Miller and Morejon unavailable. It is uncertain if Morejon will be able to pitch late in the game in another must-win contest on Wednesday in Game 4, but the Padres will at least have their stud closer back in the fold. The two-time All-Star was lights-out during the regular season, his first full season with the Friars, posting a 1.67 ERA (1.17 FIP), 0.900 WHIP, a career-high and league-high 38 saves, a career-high 129 strikeouts, and 26 walks in just 70 innings pitched. With their season on the line, expect manager Craig Stammen to be aggressive in his usage of Miller if Game 4 is close in the later innings, even though he showed command issues in the ninth on Sunday in Milwaukee.--Keith Hernandez
Source: San Diego Padres
Miguel Rojas Not Worried About Back/Hip Injury


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 12:28 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran infielder Miguel Rojas (back, hip) said he felt some tightness in his left lower-back/hip area during a swing in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday against the hosting Atlanta Braves before he was pulled mid at-bat, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. However, Rojas was not concerned about his availability for the rest of the series and going forward. Rojas probably will not be in the Dodgers' starting lineup for Game 4 of the series on Wednesday at Truist Park against Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle, but it sounds like he should be available off the bench. The 37-year-old Venezuelan infielder has made two starts so far in the NLDS against the Braves and has gone 1-for-4 with a double and a strikeout. He was hitless in three at-bats with a strikeout in Tuesday's Game 3 win before being replaced at second base by Tommy Edman. Rojas has mostly been a bench player for the Dodgers in his 13th year in the league (fourth with L.A.) in 2026, but he proved in last year's World Series that he is still capable of coming through in the clutch when needed. He hit .267 (60-for-225) with four homers and 23 RBI during the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Oct 7, 2026, 11:57 AM ET
St. Louis Cardinals right-handed closer Riley O'Brien was a first-time All-Star in 2026 in his first full season as the team's closer, and he ended the year tied with San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller for the National League lead in saves (38) with a 4.08 ERA across a career-high 64 innings pitched. O'Brien also set a career high in appearances (66) in his first full year as a big-leaguer. He did not allow an earned run in his first 13 appearances of the year and ended the first half with a 3.43 ERA and a 7.9% walk rate in 39 1/3 frames. O'Brien had 24 saves in his first 28 opportunities. But in 27 appearances after the All-Star break, O'Brien had a 5.11 ERA in 24 2/3 innings, and his walk rate rose to 14.4% while he went 14-for-18 in save chances. Three of his blown saves in the second half came in September, and five of his losing decisions came in his final 13 outings. The 31-year-old said he experienced "fatigue" in the closing days of the season and that his legs have "been feeling heavy compared to how they felt early in the year," according to Daniel Guerrero of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. As he tired, the velocity of O'Brien's pitches suffered. To be able to maintain velocity through the entire season, O'Brien said he plans to focus on putting on "as much muscle as I can."--Keith Hernandez
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Daniel Guerrero
Curtis Mead the Favorite to Start at Second Base Next Year


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Boston Red Sox infielder Curtis Mead is considered the favorite to open next season as the team's starting second baseman, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. The Red Sox acquired Mead from the Washington Nationals at the trade deadline this summer, but he ended up playing in only one game for Boston due to a fractured wrist that he suffered in his second at-bat with the team. The 25-year-old will now have all offseason to heal up, and he will enter spring training as the team's primary option at the keystone as they attempt to get back to the playoffs in 2027. The Australian native was having a breakout 2026 campaign with the Nationals before being traded to Boston, and he finished the year with a .253/.353/.498 slash line with an .851 OPS, 17 home runs, 48 RBI, 49 runs scored, and six stolen bases in 285 at-bats in 88 combined games with Washington and Boston. "That would be, I would say, broadly our plan," said manager Chad Tracy when asked about second base. "He was acquired for a reason. You see the numbers that kind of project at least toward a 30-home run season. And adding that, we were really excited about that."--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Walker Buehler to Start Game 4 of NLDS Against Brewers


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:36 AM ET
The San Diego Padres announced that veteran right-hander Walker Buehler will make the start in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers. Buehler will make his first postseason appearance this year after going 9-6 with a 4.63 ERA (4.51 FIP) and 1.35 WHIP with 131 strikeouts and 57 walks in 153 2/3 innings pitched across his 32 starts for the Padres in his first season with the team. The 32-year-old is no longer the high-end ace that he was with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he does have plenty of postseason experience, posting a 3.04 ERA (3.21 FIP) with 114 strikeouts and 36 walks in 94 2/3 innings pitched. Buehler's last start came on Sept. 26 against the division-rival Arizona Diamondbacks, when he allowed four runs (three earned) with a walk and three strikeouts in just 3 2/3 innings for a no-decision. He picked up a win in his only outing against Milwaukee in 2026, giving up just one earned run with two walks and five strikeouts in six innings at Petco Park back on Aug. 11. Buehler will most definitely be on a short leash in a must-win game for San Diego if he is not on his game early on.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Padres PR
Adrian Morejon Dealing With "Stickiness in his Shoulder"


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:28 AM ET
San Diego Padres left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon (shoulder) was unavailable in Game 3 of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on Tuesday night against the Milwaukee Brewers due to "stickiness in his shoulder," manager Craig Stammen told AJ Cassavell of MLB.com. There is still a chance that Morejon will be available for Game 4 against the Brewers in San Diego on Wednesday night as the Friars attempt to force a Game 5 back in Milwaukee on Friday night. With Morejon unavailable and closer Mason Miller on the paternity list, the Padres' bullpen was very short on Tuesday night, but Game 1 starter Michael King came to the rescue and threw the final two innings for SD to pick up a save in the 4-3 victory. Morejon has already had two two-inning appearances in this postseason, once in the Wild-Card Series against the Chicago Cubs and again on Saturday against the Brewers in Game of the NLDS, when he allowed the game-winning home run to catcher William Contreras. The hard-throwing Cuban left-hander was one of the most effective late-inning setup men during the regular season, though, going 9-3 with a 2.83 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, three saves, and a career-high 107 strikeouts in just 86 innings out of the bullpen. With Miller unlikely to be back with the team on Wednesday, the Padres could really use Morejon's left arm on Wednesday evening.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - AJ Cassavell
Oct 6, 2026, 10:58 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman was one of the stars of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday. Freeman had just one hit in four plate appearances, but it was a solo home run off Braves ace Chris Sale. Freeman put together another strong regular season in 2026, hitting .288/.362/.430 with 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 74 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. The 37-year-old's production tailed off late in the year, as he hit just .184 in September and slugged just one home run across 249 plate appearances after the All-Star break. However, Freeman has looked like his vintage self so far this postseason. Across the first three games of the NLDS, Freeman has logged four hits, two home runs, two RBI, and three runs scored.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:40 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers utility man Enrique Hernandez struck one of the big blows of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, clubbing a two-run home run off of Braves ace Chris Sale to open the scoring in the fourth inning. It was Hernandez's only hit of the night, but it helped the Dodgers chase Sale out of the game after just five innings of work. Hernandez missed a large chunk of the regular season with an oblique injury and was not particularly effective when healthy, hitting .222 with four home runs across 96 plate appearances. However, the 35-year-old has a long history as an unlikely postseason hero. Across 332 career plate appearances in the playoffs, Hernandez has now hit .272 with 18 home runs and 44 RBI.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com

item.dc:creator: Roger Rubin
item.description: The Yankees offered Paul Goldschmidt a $4 million deal to play one more season in what certainly has looked like a Hall of Fame career. item.content:encoded:
The Yankees offered Paul Goldschmidt a $4 million deal to play one more season in what certainly has looked like a Hall of Fame career. He accepted, even though he knew he would no longer be the every-day starter. The organization got a massive return on their investment as the first baseman hit 18 home runs and had 52 RBI in essentially a platoon role.
Goldschmidt was incredibly disappointed after the Yankees lost to Tampa Bay, 4-3, in the Game 3 of their AL Division Series on Wednesday night at the Stadium. But when asked about the notion of reprising the role one more time, he replied, “I'd like to continue playing, so we'll see if that opportunity happens.”
“I’ve absolutely loved my time here – I don't know if there's anyone who loved being a Yankee more than me,” Goldschmidt said. “I love the guys in this clubhouse. I love living here in New York. But you don't really know what the future holds so I think we'll just see what happens. But I can't say enough great things about this organization and my time here. We'll see what happens.”
Goldschmidt won the 2022 NL MVP Award with St. Louis and finished second in MVP voting two other times and third once while with the Diamondbacks. He has 390 home runs, an .877 OPS and four Gold Gloves for his defense.
He will be 39 next season.
Goldschmidt played in his first postseason in 2011 when he broke into the majors as Arizona lost to Milwaukee in the NL Division Series. He made the playoffs once more with the D-backs in 2017 and then three times with St. Louis from 2019 to 2021. He’s now made it twice with the Yankees but still has yet to win a World Series.
“My mindset really hasn't changed: hopefully be able to have a chance to do that again and hopefully win a championship,” he said.
Considered a good influence on the clubhouse and on the younger Yankees in particular, Goldschmidt was asked about what his message would be to the players who are beginning to form a nucleus for the years ahead.
“I think you’ve just got to keep working, but not taking this for granted either,” he said. “You don't know if you're going to get the opportunity again. You don't know what our individual careers hold. You don't know what team you'll be playing for the next year. . . . and that's what makes this so disappointing.
“But the young guys here did great. They’ve got a great head on their shoulders, very talented physically, but also mentally. They know what they're doing, and they've done a great job. Without those guys, we wouldn't be here right now. So the future is bright for them individually, and I think for this organization too.”

After being swept out of last year's NLCS, Pat Murphy and the Milwaukee Brewers look to turn the page in this year's edition with a rematch against the reigning back-to-back champion Los Angeles Dodgers.

The Dodgers and Brewers will begin their best-of-seven series on Sunday, Oct. 11. See the full schedule below.

Where will the Dodgers vs. Brewers League Championship Series be played?
Games 1 and 2 will be played in Milwaukee at American Family Field, with Games 3 and 4 moving to Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. Should the series go past four, Dodger Stadium will host Game 5 before the series heads back to Milwaukee for Games 6 and 7.
Dodgers vs. Brewers probable starting pitchers

How does the MLB League Championship Series format work?
The NLCS and ALCS are best-of-seven series. The higher seed receives home-field advantage for the series, with Games 1-2 and potential Games 6-7 hosted by the higher seed and Games 3-5 hosted by the lower seed. The first team to win four games will take the series and advance to the World Series.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Junior Caminero did a lot of elite trolling after Rays swept Yankees
item.dc:creator: Kyle Koster
item.description: To the victors go the spoils and the Tampa Bay Rays have earned every right to crow. The plucky upstarts, who happened to win the American League East with the junior circuit's best record this year, completed a three-game sweep over the mighty New York Yankees on Wednesday night to secure a spot in the ALCS. MORE: Jazz Chisholm 'confused' by Yankees' fans reaction Everything this team does well was on full display as unheralded players continuously rose to the occasion. Junior Caminero, the Ray
item.content:encoded:
To the victors go the spoils and the Tampa Bay Rays have earned every right to crow.
The plucky upstarts, who happened to win the American League East with the junior circuit's best record this year, completed a three-game sweep over the mighty New York Yankees on Wednesday night to secure a spot in the ALCS.
MORE: Jazz Chisholm 'confused' by Yankees' fans reaction
Everything this team does well was on full display as unheralded players continuously rose to the occasion. Junior Caminero, the Rays' sole superstar, went 3-for-10 in the series and worked two walks. Though he did not contribute much in the realm of power, the third baseman had plenty of energy to take up the mantle as chief trash-talker after the final out was recorded.
Caminero threw out a bit of everything in his defiant celebration. First there was the exaggerated sweeping motion to let a dejected Yankees Stadium crowd know just how thoroughly their beloved team had been beaten.
He continued the revelry by channeling David Ortiz and bellowing about the Yankees' loss.
Once in the clubhouse, his fire only burned brighter and by the time those suds-soaked interviews began, he was under the impression he was the best in the world.
There are a lot of not very fun people out there who shame baseball teams for celebrating like they've just won the World Series on every step to winning the World Series. By the time the Fall Classic wraps a squad can have four or five of these out-of-control parties under their belt.
And to be clear, most of them don't age well because only one franchise can win the whole dang thing.
But here's a rebuttal. Baseball is an insane marathon and there are thousands upon thousands of boring hours against the actual game action. Teams are together for seven or eight months and need every excuse they can to blow off some steam and celebrate what they've accomplished together.
Just think of how much Yankees fans are going to hate Caminero for his entire career now based on just a few clips. That is, if they don't use their considerable funds to take him away from small-market Tampa in a couple years. None of that would be possible without carte blanche to party it up and take every available opportunity to twist the knife.

The Los Angeles Dodgers will play for another National League pennant.
The two-time reigning World Series champions have advanced to a third straight National League Championship Series. No. 2-seeded Los Angeles took down the No. 3 Atlanta Braves in four games in the NLDS of the 2026 MLB playoffs.
Los Angeles now awaits the winner of the other NLDS matchup between the No. 1 Milwaukee Brewers and No. 4 San Diego Padres. The Dodgers are looking to pull off the rare feat of a World Series three-peat.
As the next round of the MLB postseason takes shape, here's what to know for the NLCS and ALCS:
How many games are in the ALCS, NLCS?
The remainder of the MLB postseason will feature best-of-seven series. The higher seed hosts Games 1 and 2, along with the potential Games 6 and 7.
When does the 2026 NLCS start?
The NLCS begins Sunday, Oct. 11.
What is the 2026 NLCS schedule?
The Dodgers will have home-field advantage if they face the Padres. Otherwise, the NLCS will begin in Milwaukee.

The ALCS starts Monday, Oct. 12.

No team has emerged from the ALDS just yet. The ALCS will pit the winner of the No. 1 Tampa Bay Rays-No. 4 New York Yankees series against the winner of the No. 2 Cleveland Guardians-No. 6 Chicago White Sox series.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Braves’ Ronald Acuña Jr. Undergoes MRI
item.dc:creator: Michael Whitaker

item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves are officially on the brink of elimination from the MLB postseason, trailing two games to one in their National League Division Series against the reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers.
Meanwhile, right fielder Ronald Acuña Jr. recently underwent an MRI after experiencing soreness in his right knee after getting shaken up during a stolen base attempt in their Game 2 win.
The good news for the Braves is that he was given the all-clear and will be in the lineup for Wednesday's elimination contest.
Atlanta Braves Infielder Ronald Acuña Jr. Underwent An MRI
During Game 3 against the Dodgers, Acuña Jr. was originally scheduled to bat second in the order and play right field, but was moved to the designated hitter position because of the lingering soreness in his knee.
He went 0-for-3 with a walk and a strikeout.
The Braves Don't Appear To Be Worried By His Slump
Earlier in the series, the Braves weren't making much of his slump, simply saying they just need him to play to the best of his abilities.
"We just need Ronald to be Ronald," Braves ace Chris Sale said via MLB.com. "I'll be honest, 50 percent of him is better than most. I think going back home might alleviate a little bit of that pressure, being in front of our home fans, and just staying loose. I think you get into these situations, and sometimes you try to do more."
"I don't worry about him just because the talent is so big that it's going to show up," Braves manager Walt Weiss said.
Meanwhile, Acuña Jr. said that he thrives on the pressure.
"I love it when I face the pitchers that are superstars," Acuña said. "Every time I go to the plate to compete. We're trying to win. So I'm doing my best. As you know, these pitches, they're nasty."
The Braves have no choice but to win on Wednesday in order to extend their season.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Braves' Ronald Acuña Jr. Undergoes MRI appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are one loss in the American League Division Series away from elimination, and fans online are calling for the team to move on from Aaron Boone.
Since Boone took over, the Yankees have only been to one World Series and have lost the American League Championship Series twice. The Yankees spend a ton of money, and the expectation that comes with the uniform is a World Series, year in and year out. Whether that is fair or not is another story, but it does not change the fact that the Yankees have underachieved under Boone despite having great teams every season.
Before Wednesday's do-or-die game, Cody Bellinger sang praises of his manager.
"Boone is a great guy to play for," Bellinger told reporters before the game. "I've played for four really good managers, in my opinion, and my transition over here was smooth. It's all about winning here. When you put on this logo, it's all about winning. We understand what comes with the logo, what comes with the history. He helps present that."
Bellinger thinks Boone has done a great job setting the expectations for what it means to be a Yankee. However, the team has failed to meet those expectations, and fans have a right to be upset.
Boone has one more year on his deal, and he will reportedly not be fired regardless of this year's outcome. In his defense, he did manage most of this season without Aaron Judge, which certainly made a huge impact. A healthy Judge could have drastically changed the outlook of this season.

item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves enter Game 4 of the NLDS with their season on the line after falling behind 2-1 in the series against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Atlanta was fortunate to split the first two games at Dodger Stadium before they dropped Game 3 at Truist Park. Now facing elimination, there is more pressure than ever for the Braves' offense to break through.
The Braves' offense struggled mightily in Game 3 against 2025 World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Yamamoto went seven innings, allowing only one run and recording 10 strikeouts. The Braves would go on to record only one hit over the following two innings against Tanner Scott and Edwin Diaz.
Atlanta has yet to score more than three runs in the series, but the team's biggest bats will need to deliver on Wednesday against right-hander Tyler Glasnow. Braves third baseman Austin Riley is one of the hitters still trying to find his footing in the series.
No Panic in Atlanta
Riley, a two-time All-Star, is 0-for-10 with five strikeouts through the first three games of the series. Despite facing elimination and his own struggles at the plate, Riley is not panicking ahead of a critical Game 4.
"We're still very confident. It's a confident clubhouse. We think we can get the job done and take this thing to LA. We've just got to go out there and play clean baseball and capitalize on the opportunities when it presents itself," Riley said, according to Barrett Sallee of the Braves Radio Network.
Riley's confidence will need to translate into results immediately if the Braves are to keep their season alive. The Braves cannot afford to waste scoring chances against a Dodgers pitching staff that has controlled the majority of this series.
Far From His Best
Sep 29, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Braves third baseman Austin Riley (27) reacts after hitting a three run home run against the Philadelphia Phillies in the eighth inning during game one of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Riley's difficult series at the plate comes following his worst statistical season of his career. In 159 games this year, he is slashing .219/.290/.364 for a career-worst .654 OPS with 19 home runs and 72 RBIs.
Despite a challenging year, Riley has shown flashes of his All-Star self this postseason. In Game 1 of the Wild Card Series against the Philadelphia Phillies, Riley hit a three-run, go-ahead home run in the eighth inning to flip the momentum Atlanta's way en route to a Game 1 victory.
With the Braves on the brink of elimination, Wednesday's Game 4 would be a perfect time for another one of those game-changing moments.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Why Phillies Trying to Trade Trea Turner Feels Impossible
item.dc:creator: Nick Ziegler; Unknown

item.content:encoded:
As the Philadelphia Phillies prepare for the offseason, the team is going to have a lot of different areas to address.
Coming off a disappointing year by their standards, what the Phillies do this offseason is going to be interesting to watch. Philadelphia is a team that has pulled off the impressive feat of being able to reach the postseason for five straight years.
While many teams would be pleased with that feat, the Phillies are a franchise that has World Series or bust expectations. Philadelphia has a high payroll and a lot of star power. Unfortunately, it really hasn’t panned out of late.
Now, with another year of being eliminated early in October, there is a possibility that the team will look to shake things up. There have already been some rumblings that big names could be available for the Phillies, and not surprisingly, Trea Turner’s name has been mentioned.
However, coming off a bad season with a massive contract, trading him seems like it could be an impossible task for Philadelphia.
Trying to Trade Turner Seems Impossible
One of the reasons why the lineup didn’t live up to their expectations this season was because of the performance of Turner. The former All-Star shortstop had the worst year of his career, slashing .242/.297/.378 with 18 home runs, 58 RBI, and 21 stolen bases; it was the lowest OPS that he had in a proper season.
At 33 years old, the down season at the plate should be seen as a major concern for the team. Furthermore, while the offensive numbers weren’t good, neither was his play defensively.
There has to be some conversation this offseason about him switching positions. Shortstop is too important on the field not to have a good defender there, and Turner struggled a lot.
While the Phillies might look to shop him this winter, it is hard to imagine that it would gain any traction. At 33 years old, struggling defensively, having the worst year of his career at the plate, and the massive contact he has makes it seem like he would be one of the hardest players in the league to trade.
The 33-year-old still has seven years at just over $27 million left on his contract. Unless the Phillies were to eat a significant amount of this deal, it’s hard to imagine that any team would be interested. While it’s not impossible, it's safe to say that it’s highly improbable that Philadelphia will be able to move him.
Nick Ziegler is an alumnus of the Connecticut School of Broadcasting. He has been working in sports media covering the NFL, NBA, MLB, and NHL for nearly a decade with various publications online. With his free time, Nick enjoys being at the Jersey Shore with his wife, daughter, and their golden retriever. You can follow him on X, formerly Twitter, @NickZiegler20.

item.content:encoded:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses the calculus the Red Sox have to make when considering a potential contract extension for All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. Be sure to join out FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
The Boston Red Sox made a massive gamble ahead of the trade deadline, sending a massive haul of prospects to the Baltimore Orioles in exchange for three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. After underperforming in 32 games with Boston, Rutschman now enters his final year of salary arbitration. But the Red Sox face a tough decision on whether to try to extend Rutschman ahead of the 2027 season.
Here's what a potential extension could look like:
What is Rutschman looking for?
Prior to being traded to Boston, Rutschman had exploratory talks with Baltimore about a potential extension. "Rutschman, then, would probably want a deal that makes him a lifetime Oriole, or close to it," wrote The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal on July 6. "His benchmark might be the nine-year, $167 million extension Buster Posey signed with the San Francisco Giants in March 2013," he continued.
The idea that Rutschman could be in line for a deal like Posey's, who will almost assuredly be in Cooperstown in the near future, is a bit far-fetched. Prior to signing that deal, Posey posted a career slash line of .314/.380/.503/.883 with 46 home runs and 191 RBI, winning the 2010 National League Rookie of the Year award, the 2012 National League Most Valuable Player award, and two World Series titles. A far cry from Rutschman's .252/.339/.414/.753 with 74 home runs and 290 RBI, with a career accolade list of three All-Star appearances.
Catchers typically struggle to capitalize on their value given the high injury risk from the wear and tear of being behind the plate nightly. Rutschman is no stranger to those concerns, having played just 189 games over the last two seasons.
Beyond Rutschman's worse resume than Posey's, the Red Sox have shied away from deals that take players well into their 30s, with the longest deal in recent memory being the eight-year extension given to Roman Anthony, which takes him through his age-29 season.
Comparisons
With Posey's nine-year deal seemingly out the window, we'll have to look at some more recent catcher deals, which… gets complicated, to say the least. Of the five richest deals signed by catchers, only one was signed with one year of service time remaining: Toronto Blue Jays' Alejandro Kirk. So let's start there:
Kirk
Ahead of the 2026 season, Kirk signed a five-year, $58-million deal to remain in Toronto through 2030. Before signing, Kirk was a two-time All-Star with a career line of .268/.345/.398/.743. Like Rutschman, Kirk is a strong defensive catcher when it comes to blocking balls in the dirt and framing. However, he struggles to throw runners out.
Though an average annual value of $11.6 million feels low based on Rosenthal's reporting, we'll have to keep looking.
Sean Murphy
At 29, Murphy signed a six-year, $73-million extension with the Atlanta Braves, buying out his final two years of arbitration. According to Spotrac, Murphy was paid $9 million in 2024, his penultimate arbitration year, and $15 million annually for the remainder of the deal.
At the time of signing, Murphy posted a .240/.336/.441/.778 line with 67 home runs and 215 RBI, earning an All-Star selection and becoming one of the game's best defensive catchers.
Cal Raleigh
The runner-up for the 2025 American League Most Valuable Player award, Raleigh signed a six-year, $105-million deal to remain with the Seattle Mariners through the 2030 season, buying out his final three arbitration years. In the four seasons leading up to his extension, Raleigh posted a line of .218/.296/.444/.740 with 93 home runs and 251 RBI. Defensively. Raleigh is a mixed bag, with improving blocking skills, but is middle of the road in both framing and throwing runners out.
Raleigh's deal is also slightly different than the one Rutschman would be looking to sign. While his deal carries an AAV of $17.5 million, the number is lower because he's receiving a lower salary in what would have been his arbitration years. Beginning in 2028, Raleigh will be paid $24.6 million annually.
Will Smith
Will Smith of the Los Angeles Dodgers has the richest catcher contract (by total value). Smith signed a 10-year, $140-million extension with Los Angeles ahead of the 2024 season, buying out his final two arbitration years. However, in typical Dodgers fashion, Smith will be paid $5 million annually from 2034-2043 in deferred payments, lowering the luxury tax hit to just $12 million annually. The deferred payments, expected to be a hot-button topic in ongoing labor talks, paired with Smith being paid through his age-38 season, make the comparison a bit far-fetched.
Before signing the deal, Smith hit .261/.357/.483/.840 with 91 home runs and 306 RBI over five seasons, while providing slightly above-average defense behind the plate.
So... Where does Rutschman fall?
Projecting contracts is an imperfect science. From a strictly production standpoint, Rutschman is most similar to Murphy or Kirk. However, neither player dealt with the same injury problems as Rutschman in the seasons leading up to their extensions. Murphy also represents the closest fit defensively to Rutschman, profiling as one of the best defensive catchers in the sport. The $15 million AAV Murphy would earn from 2025 through 2028 would seem to be the floor of what Rutschman would look for in a potential deal. With MLB Trade Rumors projecting Rutschman to make $9 million in arbitration in 2027, could the Red Sox bump that number up slightly to lower the value of the remainder of the deal to, say, $11 million in 2027 and $14-15 million each year after?
Then, of course, comes the term: catchers especially struggle to cash in on the open market later in their careers. Philadelphia Phillies backstop JT Realmuto posted a line of .257/.315/.384/.700 in 134 games in 2025 before hitting the open market ahead of his age-35 season. Realmuto sat on the free-agent market until Jan. 20, when he signed a three-year, $45-million extension to return to Philadelphia, a move widely criticized as an overpay for a catcher his age.
Red Sox Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow will have to get creative to find common ground with Rutschman. A six-year contract would take him through his age-34 season, having him hit the market at a rather inopportune time. One possible solution for the Red Sox to give Rutschman the long-term commitment he's reportedly seeking could be to front-load the deal, paying him more in his prime while paying him incrementally less as he ages, reducing the franchise's financial burden as he ages and presumably declines.

The 2026 MLB playoffs have arrived!
The 12-team postseason began with an action-packed wild-card round that featured eight teams battling for four spots to advance to the eight-team division series.
The Chicago White Sox became the first team to win a series this postseason with a wild-card round sweep of the Houston Astros. Then the New York Yankees swept the Boston Red Sox in two routs, recording the highest series run differential in the history of the current wild-card format. The San Diego Padresalso sealed their spot in the NLDS with a sweep of the Chicago Cubs. In the only wild-card series to go the distance, the Atlanta Braves held off the Philadelphia Philliesto move on.
From the first pitch of the wild-card games to the last out of the World Series, we've got you covered with the postseason bracket, schedules, results and how to watch every game this October.

item.content:encoded:
How Braves' Ronald Acuna Jr. has impressed analyst despite quiet playoffs showing appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Atlanta Braves won the 2021 World Series without Ronald Acuna Jr., but they are unlikely to go all the way in 2026 unless the franchise pillar comes alive in the playoffs. He was hitting just .167 with a .485 OPS through his last 18 at-bats entering Tuesday's National League Division Series battle versus the Los Angeles Dodgers. One broadcaster is not worried, however.
"He's been okay in the postseason — he hasn't been the superstar yet — but we feel like his moment is coming. Sooner than later," Braves color analyst C.J. Nitkowski told the "Foul Territory" podcast. "The thing I have been impressed with is he's not necessarily become a guy who's pressing. There are times you're watching at-bats and you know he wants to do something big, and you're thinking 'man, he's going to chase here.' And he doesn't.
"He's been under control. It hasn't happened for him just yet… but nobody's worried about the health of Ronald Acuna Jr. {or} his ability to put up big moments here in the postseason."
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Ronald Acuña Jr. has wisely avoided pressing in big moments, and it's caught @CJNitkowski's eye…
"He hasn't been the superstar yet, but we feel like his moment is coming sooner rather than later." pic.twitter.com/AJSdOfJVi1
— Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) October 6, 2026
Players live and die by their approach in this sport, and if their process proves successful, the hits will come. The prodigiously talented Acuna believes he will deliver for the Braves when they need him most. Former MVP Award winners tend to be confident, and for good reason. He eventually erupted in the regular season, and fans are trusting him to do the same in October.
Acuna has endured his struggles during this time of the year, however. He owns a .769 OPS through 34 playoff games, which is nearly 130 points lower than his career output. That still might be enough to help Atlanta move forward.
The 28-year-old right fielder is eying his first extra-base hit of the 2026 postseason during a pivotal Game 3 NLDS clash. Ronald Acuna Jr. is still finding ways to contribute, scoring a run in his four previous games, but one big knock could open the flood gates in Truist Park.

item.content:encoded:
The National League’s top-seeded Milwaukee Brewers head to San Diego, California, with a 2-0 lead in their NLDS matchup against the Padres for Game 3 Tuesday night at Petco Park. The Brewers have a chance to advance to the NLCS for the second consecutive year with a win, while the Padres will be fighting to keep their season alive with the help of their home crowd.
The Brewers earned a first-round bye as the No. 1 seed in the NL and home-field advantage throughout the MLB playoffs after finishing the regular season with the best record in the league. While that extra time off during the Wild Card Series has hurt teams with a first-round bye plenty of times in the past, it hasn’t slowed down Milwaukee, which won the first two games of the NLDS against San Diego.
Both games have been one-run contests so far, with Brewers catcher William Contreras playing the hero in Game 1 with his go-ahead solo home run in the seventh inning as Milwaukee went on to win 3-2. The Brewers followed that with a dramatic 4-3 victory in Game 2 when 22-year-old outfielder Jackson Chourio delivered a walk-off two-RBI single against Padres superstar closer Mason Miller.
The Brewers are giving the start to right-hander Dustin May for Game 3. May went 7-9 with a 4.70 ERA across 31 regular season starts between Milwaukee and St. Louis. Tuesday night will be May’s first playoff appearance since he appeared in seven games with the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2020.
The Padres will counter with right-hander Nick Pivetta, who missed a large portion of the season due to injury before making his return on Sept. 7. He posted a 2-0 record with a 1.45 ERA across four starts in September and has pitched really well for San Diego since signing with the team ahead of the 2025 season, owning a 16-7 record with a 2.87 ERA and 0.99 WHIP over the last two regular seasons. Pivetta already made a start for the Padres in the NL Wild Card Series, allowing one run over 3.1 innings against the Chicago Cubs on Sept. 30.
Check out Brewers vs. Padres MLB playoff predictions, picks, and more below ahead of Tuesday night’s NLDS Game 3 at Petco Park.
Brewers vs. Padres Odds for Game 3
Hard Rock Bet Sportsbook lists the Padres as favorites for Game 3 as they return home with their season on the line:
- Moneyline: Padres -140, Brewers +115
- Run Line: Padres -1.5 (+155), Brewers +1.5 (-190)
- Total (Runs): Over 7.5 (-110), Under 7.5 (-110)
Brewers vs. Padres NLDS Winner Odds
The Padres are listed as favorites for Game 3 Tuesday night, but with the Brewers leading the series 2-0 and needing only one more win to advance, Hard Rock Bet Sportsbook lists Milwaukee as a significant favorite to win the NLDS:
- Brewers to Win NLDS: -950
- Padres to Win NLDS: +600
Brewers vs. Padres MLB Playoff Predictions
Don’t forget to check out the Stats Hub at Hard Rock Bet Sportsbook, where you can find our Brewers vs. Padres MLB playoff prediction below, which uses baseball betting insights and trends to support the pick:
Padres vs. Brewers Best Bet: Fernando Tatís Jr. Over 0.5 Runs (-105)
Fernando Tatís Jr. is the tone-setter at the top of the Padres’ lineup, and when a dynamic player like him who’s a major threat on the base paths reaches safely, there’s a good chance he’ll end up coming around to score. Tatís’ 96 runs scored during the regular season were near the top of MLB, and while it’s still a small sample size, his four runs scored during the playoffs so far are tied for the second-most.
Tatís is batting only .176 this postseason, but he has a stolen base and has scored the four runs mentioned above. He scored three runs in the Padres’ Game 1 win over the Cubs in the NL Wild Card Series and then scored a run in Game 2 of the NLDS this past Sunday. Tatís has also scored at least one run in three of his last five games dating back to the regular season.
- Padres vs. Brewers Player Prop Pick for NLDS Game 3: Fernando Tatís Jr. Over 0.5 Runs (-105)
Top 5 Most-Bet Player Props for MIL-SD
Jackson Chourio was the hero in Game 2 for the Brewers and has recorded a hit in each of the first two games of this series, making his hits prop the most-bet player prop for Game 3 of the NLDS against the Padres:
- Jackson Chourio – Over 0.5 Hits
- Fernando Tatís Jr. – Over 0.5 Home Runs
- Manny Machado – Over 0.5 Hits
- Dustin May – Over 2.5 Strikeouts
- Ty France – Over 0.5 Hits
Brewers vs. Padres Betting Splits for Game 3
Here’s how the action is trending at Hard Rock Bet for Tuesday night’s potential elimination game in the NLDS at Petco Park:
- The Padres are drawing more moneyline support with 58.6% of bets and an even higher 71.7% of the dollars.
- The Brewers are generating more action on the run line with 61.5% of bets, but San Diego accounts for 56.3% of the dollars.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers' William Contreras ghosted agent for weeks after Braves trade appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Up 2-0 in their NL Division Series (NLDS) matchup against the San Diego Padres, the Milwaukee Brewers are on the precipice of another NL Championship Series (NLCS) berth. A Game 3 win over the Padres Tuesday night would give the Brewers home-field advantage against the winner of the Los Angeles Dodgers-Atlanta Braves NLDS tilt. On Tuesday, Milwaukee catcher William Contreras appeared on a podcast with former Braves teammate Ronald Acuna Jr. Contreras told his agent to not speak to him for three weeks once the news broke he was heading to Milwaukee, shared by X (formerly Twitter) user Master Flip.
William Contreras stopped talking to his agent for 3 weeks after the Braves traded him to Milwaukee 😳
Acuña: “Did it hurt when you were traded?”
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Contreras: “Of course, bro. I got over it, but when I got here to Milwaukee in 2024, the vibe wasn’t the same, and I was like, damn.… pic.twitter.com/HAv3ZgXINh
— Master Flip | Phillip Feliz 🇩🇴 (@Masterflip_) October 6, 2026
"December 15th, traded to Milwaukee, and it hit," Contreras stated to his former teammate. "I stopped talking to my agent. I told him, don't text me for 3 weeks; I don't want to talk to you. He tells me no, that it's business, and I said that's not business at all. I kept telling him, send me back to Atlanta. I just thought about the guys there because it was a vibe."
As the NL's top seed, there's a good chance that the Brewers could host the Braves in the NLCS. A win on the road Tuesday night would give the Brew Crew some rest before facing off against either prospective opponent. Last year, the Dodgers dispatched the Brewers in a clean sweep. A match against the Braves would likely favor Milwaukee, who is looking to get back to the World Series for the first time since 1982.
In any case, it looks like Contreras is right at home with the Brewers. He's become a multiple-time All-Star and one of baseball's best all-around catchers. Despite a breakout 2022 campaign, the Braves elected to trade for Athletics All-Star Sean Murphy, sending Contreras up north a few days later. Murphy has declined in Atlanta, mostly due to injuries. 2025 NL Rookie of the Year Drake Baldwin has replaced him. Can Contreras lead the Brew Crew back to the Fall Classic? If so, the trade will have paid off quite well in Milwaukee.
Related: Padres go to extreme lengths to mess with Brewers before do-or-die NLDS Game 3

item.content:encoded:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses the calculus the Red Sox have to make when considering a potential contract extension for All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. Be sure to join out FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
Aside from the back-to-back World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers landing back-to-back American League Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, the Boston Red Sox made the biggest splash at the trade deadline, landing three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman. With only one season of team control remaining, should the Red Sox extend the 28-year-old backstop?
It took a massive haul of prospects to acquire Rutschman from the division rival Baltimore Orioles, including pitchers Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon, outfielders Enddy Azocar and Harold Rivas, and Carlos Narvaez, Boston's former starting catcher. After being ranked as a top-10 farm system in the sport ahead of the deadline, the Red Sox saw their farm system fall into the bottom 10 as a result of the trade.
Rutschman was a mixed bag in his first two months in a Red Sox uniform, battling both wrist and elbow issues that saw him in and out of the lineup. After hitting just .187/.253/.363/.615 in his first 25 games in Boston, he ended the regular season hitting .333/.355/.567/.922 in the final seven games.
In 32 regular season games, the 28-year-old hit .222/.278/.410/.688 for Boston. Despite the rough numbers, he was one of the few Red Sox players to get a hit during the team's Wild Card series loss to the New York Yankees, going 1-for-8. Given the cost of acquisition, it's safe to say it was an underwhelming outcome for him at the plate.
However, he was incredibly impressive defensively, particularly with the ABS challenge system. In 34 challenges, Rutschman went 24-10, a 71 percent success rate. Every other Boston catcher went a combined 73-48, good for a 60 percent success rate. Rutschman was a noticeable upgrade over Narvaez, who went 32-27, a 54 percent success rate.
While Rutschman was a mixed bag, the prospect haul it took to acquire him all took off after joining their new organization. For Eyanson and Azocar, it was a continuation of breakout seasons that began in Boston. For Witherspoon, it was his first taste of success in professional baseball after struggling in Boston.
Eyanson, the No. 45-rated prospect in baseball, per MLB Pipeline, posted a 2.03 ERA in six starts with Baltimore's Double-A affiliate Chesapeake. He finished the season with a 1.82 ERA over 79 innings across two levels en route to being named a finalist for the Minor League Pitcher of the Year Award, which went to his former LSU teammate, Seattle Mariners starter Kade Anderson.
After hitting .286/.341/.550/.891 with 18 home runs and 27 doubles while driving in 63 runs, while playing excellent outfield defense in 85 games with Single-A Salem and High-A Greenville, Azocar was one of the biggest risers in the Red Sox system in 2026. His breakout season continued in Baltimore, where he hit .327/.372/.529/.901 with three home runs and eight doubles in 25 games for High-A Frederick. After a breakout season, Azocar now ranks No. 99 in MLB Pipeline's top 100 prospects.
It was a rocky first professional season for Witherspoon, the Red Sox first-round selection in the 2025 MLB Draft. The 21-year-old posted a 4.78 ERA in 17 starts with Greenville before being dealt to Baltimore. However, whatever changes the Orioles made seemed to click, as he allowed only two earned runs in his final three starts.
While Rutschman's numbers in his first two months in Boston don't necessarily warrant a long-term extension, giving up such a substantial prospect package to acquire him puts the Red Sox in a bit of a corner.
If the team waits until next season to see how he performs, they risk him not being interested in signing a deal and instead waiting for free agency, where multiple suitors will assuredly be interested. However, he's likely to command a sizable deal even before hitting the open market, one that, at least based on his time in Boston, he hasn't totally earned.
Red Sox Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow was asked about potential extension talks between the two sides in Monday's end-of-season press conference, but he offered a nonanswer and instead praised him for his work with the pitching staff.
"Adley stepped in as our primary catcher in the middle of the season, which is not easy to do, especially when pitching is a strength of our team, and immediately endeared himself to the pitching staff, to the coaching staff, to the clubhouse, just a really, really high-quality teammate and leader," Breslow said. "I think that's something we'll develop internally, and any conversations about what Adley's future will look like will take place between Adley's representatives, Adley, and me," he said about a potential extension.
It'll be an interesting calculus for Breslow to make; the initial deal to acquire Rutschman appears to be a mistake after he underperformed and you once again failed to make a deep playoff run. However, a contract extension could compound that mistake, locking in a player who has failed to stay healthy and underperformed in each of the last two seasons.

item.content:encoded:
By splitting the first two games of the National League Division Series, Atlanta essentially turned a five-game series into a three-game series -- and, oh, by the way, stole home-field advantage from the Dodgers in the process.
Next up, each team will turn to its respective staff ace in a pivotal Game 3 as the series shifts to Truist Park on Tuesday night.
“We know it's two good teams going at it,” Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman said. “We know what's at stake on Tuesday. We need to get that win.”
Just how badly does each team need that win? Consider this: In postseason history, the Game 3 winner in a best-of-five series tied 1-1 has gone on to win the series 48 of 67 times (71.6%).
Here’s everything you need to know ahead of the crucial Game 3:
When is the game and how can I watch it?
First pitch for Game 3 is set for 6 p.m. ET/3 p.m. PT on Tuesday at Truist Park. It will be broadcast on FS1/FOX Deportes/FOX One.
All series are available in the US on MLB.TV with authentication to a participating Pay TV provider. Games are also available live internationally, although not in Canada. Sportsnet is MLB's exclusive English-language broadcaster in Canada for every Postseason game, while TVA Sports will be covering the entire AL Postseason and the World Series in French and Broadcaster RDS will cover the entire NL Postseason in French.
Who are the starting pitchers?
Dodgers: RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto   
Key stat: 0.87 WHIP, ranked second among qualified MLB starters
The reigning World Series MVP is set for his 2026 postseason debut with his team looking to reclaim its series lead. Yamamoto could have started Game 1, but the Dodgers liked the way they were lined up for the NLDS and beyond with Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell starting the first two contests. L.A.'s ace is up third as the series shifts to Atlanta, where he gave up one run across 6 1/3 strong innings on Aug. 27; he was outdueled by Sale in a 1-0 loss.
Braves: LHP Chris Sale   
Key stat:  1.96 ERA over his final 24 regular-season starts
Sale will face the Dodgers for the first time since throwing a five-hit shutout against them on Aug. 27. The 37-year-old posted MLB’s third-best ERA (2.16) this year. He began the postseason by limiting the Phillies to three runs over 6 1/3 innings in Game 1 of the NL Wild Card Series. There was some thought about having him start Game 2, but because he recorded the final four outs of Game 3 of the WC Series, the Braves pushed him back.
What are the starting lineups?
Dodgers: The big change for LA's Game 3 lineup is Shohei Ohtani in the No. 5 spot. Until Tuesday, Ohtani, recovering from right biceps and left knee injuries, had not been fifth or lower in a starting lineup since Sept. 23, 2020. With Sale on the mound, the Dodgers are not only stacking the top half of their lineup mostly with right-handed hitters, they're shaking up their typical starting nine. They already started Miguel Rojas at third base over Max Muncy when facing a lefty opener in Game 2, so it's not a surprise to see Kiké Hernández getting his first start this postseason at the hot corner, shifting Rojas to second.
Braves: Drake Baldwin’s leadoff homer accounted for the game’s only run the last time the Braves faced Yamamoto. Baldwin, Matt Olson and Michael Harris II should all enjoy seeing a right-handed starter. The Braves had faced a lefty starter in four of their first five postseason games. Aaron Nola, the only right-hander they’ve seen, lasted just 1 2/3 innings in Game 3 of the NLWC Series.
How will the bullpens line up after the starter?
Braves: Coming off an off-day, the Braves will have closer Raisel Iglesias and two top setup men, Robert Suarez and Dylan Lee, available. Didier Fuentes and Ray Kerr won’t be available after both threw 40-plus pitches on Sunday.
Dodgers: The bullpen had to cover the final 5 1/3 innings of Game 2 after a shaky start from Snell, but after a series off-day, the Dodgers should have almost everyone available for Game 3. The exception may be Roki Sasaki, who threw two innings on 36 pitches on Sunday.
Any injuries of note?
Dodgers: Ohtani (right biceps, left knee) and Freeman (right knee) are managing lingering injuries. World Series hero Will Klein (right elbow discomfort) has faced hitters, but he has not pitched in a game since July 31 and is viewed as more of a depth option. Blake Treinen (right shoulder inflammation) is unlikely to pitch this postseason.
Who is hot and who is not?
Braves: Harris has two three-hit efforts in five games this postseason and is 8-for-20 (.400) overall. The Braves hope to get Acuña (3-for-18 without an extra-base hit) and Olson (3-for-19 with seven strikeouts) going as the series goes on.
Dodgers: After a tough September, Freeman (3-for-7, home run) swung the bat well in the first two games. Pages (0-for-7) and Tommy Edman (0-for-5) are seeking their first hits this postseason.
Anything else fans might want to know?
- This will be the first time Sale has faced the Dodgers in the postseason since coming out of the Red Sox bullpen to pitch a perfect ninth inning to conclude the 2018 World Series.
- Roberts enters Game 3 one win shy of 71 managerial postseason wins, which would tie Tony La Russa for second-most all-time. Joe Torre holds the record with 84.

item.title: [Heavy.com] Atlanta Braves Announce Strange Ha-Seong Kim News During NLDS vs Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Caleb Kerney
item.description: The Atlanta Braves have an opportunity to break the 1-1 tie and take the lead in their NLDS series against the reigning MLB World Series Champions. Prior to taking on the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Braves announced news about Ha-Seong Kim. Game 3 features a pitching matchup for the ages. Chris Sale takes the mound for the Braves, fresh off a 3-2 win that evened the series. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is the starter for the Dodgers. Game 3 will start at 4:00 PM Mountain Time, 3:00 PM Pacific Time, or 6:00 P
item.content:encoded:
The Atlanta Braves have an opportunity to break the 1-1 tie and take the lead in their NLDS series against the reigning MLB World Series Champions. Prior to taking on the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Braves announced news about Ha-Seong Kim.
Game 3 features a pitching matchup for the ages. Chris Sale takes the mound for the Braves, fresh off a 3-2 win that evened the series. Yoshinobu Yamamoto is the starter for the Dodgers.
Game 3 will start at 4:00 PM Mountain Time, 3:00 PM Pacific Time, or 6:00 PM Eastern Time.
Atlanta Braves Announce Ha-Seong Kim & Lane Thomas News Before NLDS Game 3 vs. the Los Angeles Dodgers
Before the first pitch of Game 3 in the NLDS between the Braves and Dodgers, the Braves announced news regarding Kim. This announcement is in regard to his placement in the lineup for the game.
Here is the lineup that the Braves announced prior to the game:
- C: Drake Baldwin
- RF: Ronald Acuna Jr.
- 1B: Matt Olson
- 2B: Ozzie Albies
- CF: Michael Harris II
- LF: Mauricio Dubon
- DH: Sean Murphy
- 3B: Austin Riley
- SS: Ha-Seong Kim
Starting Pitcher: Chris Sale
As you can see, the Braves are going with a near-identical lineup for Game 3. However, the biggest change is pulling Lane Thomas and inserting Kim.
After that, the only other change is moving Dubon from shortstop to LF (to cover the removed Thomas).
Kim is a 30-year-old infielder who played 51 regular-season games. Thomas is a 31-year-old outfielder who came over to the Braves in a trade with the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline.
Reaction To Atlanta Braves Game 3 Lineup
MLB insider Mark Bowman tried to explain today’s lineup decisions.
“Rowdy isn’t in today’s lineup. This weekend, Walt said he likes to have Murphy at DH and Baldwin at C because it allows him to PH for Murph at the right point of a game,” Bowman wrote.
A curious fan brought up an argument, and Bowman responded.
“But why wouldn’t he stack as many LHH as possible in the starting lineup against a tough righty? Could have gone Dubon at SS, Yaz in LF, Tellez at DH…..” the fan wrote.
Bowman replied with some stats regarding Yamamoto: “Yamamoto vs. RHH .586 OPS vs. LHH .510 OPS.”
Looking At Ha-Seong Kim & Lane Thomas
Kim has yet to find success during this postseason run.
Despite playing three games and earning four at-bats, he has yet to record a hit. However, he has recorded a single run, thanks to one of his two walks.
During the regular season, Kim had more offensive success.
In his 51 games, Kim recorded 15 hits, one double, one triple, nine RBIs, 16 walks, and two stolen bases to go along with a .116 batting average.
Thomas, on the other hand, hasn’t experienced much more success than Kim. He has 73 hits, 19 doubles, 40 RBIs, 44 walks, nine stolen bases, and 11 home runs in 118 games.
Additionally, he has a .224 batting average.
It looks like this change could simply be to give Thomas a night off and make sure that Kim gets a game. Because if the Braves were trying to make sure everyone in the lineup could contribute offensively, this is a strange choice.
One way or another, the Braves need to get a win to turn the tides in their favor and take a lead in the series before Game 4.

item.dc:creator: Gavin Groe
item.description: Ronald Acuña Jr. is one of the most electrifying players in baseball. The Atlanta Braves right fielder is off to a slow start in the playoffs with just three hits in 18 at-bats, but he is capable of changing a game with one swing and the Braves are counting on him to do exactly that. The winner puts the other club on the brink of elimination. Ac
item.content:encoded:
Ronald Acuña Jr. is one of the most electrifying players in baseball. The Atlanta Braves right fielder is off to a slow start in the playoffs with just three hits in 18 at-bats, but he is capable of changing a game with one swing and the Braves are counting on him to do exactly that.
It is a small sample size. Atlanta has played just five postseason games and is set to take on the Los Angeles Dodgers on Tuesday in Game 3 of the NLDS. The winner puts the other club on the brink of elimination.
Acuña entered the postseason on a tear. In September, the 28-year-old posted a .307 batting average, .347 on-base percentage, .949 OPS, seven home runs and 19 RBIs.
Off the field, Acuña has been busy as well. This year, he debuted his own podcast called La Bestia, interviewing MLB players throughout the season. He recently released an episode in which he announced his plans for the upcoming offseason.
Acuña shared that he plans to work once again with Fernando Tatis Sr., the father of San Diego Padres right fielder Fernando Tatis Jr., this winter.
"I'm going to train throughout the entire offseason with Fernando Tatis Sr. Now that he's in La Guaira, I'm going to head to the stadium every day," Acuña said, via MLB reporter Wilder Sanchez. He added, "The year I won MVP, I trained during the offseason with him."
Ronald Acuña Jr. volverá a trabajar con Fernando Tatis Sr 😱
“La Bestia” tiene como objetivo ganar el MVP en 2027 y repetirá una fórmula que ya le dio resultados en el pasado.
“Voy a practicar durante toda la offseason con Fernando Tatis Sr. Ahora que está en La Guaira voy a… pic.twitter.com/e1jvZZhr8X
— Wilber Sánchez (@wilberdata) October 6, 2026
That year was 2023, when Acuña won the National League MVP unanimously while becoming the first player in MLB history to hit 40 home runs and steal 70 bases in the same season.
Acuña is not in the offseason yet, but he is already making clear that he wants to return to the best version of himself in 2027.
He dealt with a recurring left hamstring strain this year and his overall numbers were not at the level he has set for himself. Going back to the trainer who helped him reach his peak is a smart career move.
For now though, the focus is on the Dodgers. A big Game 3 from Acuña could change the entire series.

item.content:encoded:
Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong wins impressive award ahead of likely MVP appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Chicago Cubs star Pete Crow-Armstrong is likely going to win the National League MVP Award. Although the Cubs stumbled in the first round of the postseason, PCA turned in an electric regular season. He became the seventh player in MLB history to record a 40/40 season, and Crow-Armstrong achieved many other impressive feats as well. The Cubs star received an award before his expected MVP honor on Tuesday, however. Baseball America named PCA its 2026 MLB Player of the Year.
Cubs centerfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong is Baseball America's 2026 MLB Player of the Year ⭐
PCA became the seventh member of the 40 HR / 40 SB club this season, en route to leading MLB in HR (45), R (119) and OPS (1.065).
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
In the 28-year history of BA's MLB Player of the Year… pic.twitter.com/B6hXHhfc9J
— Baseball America (@BaseballAmerica) October 6, 2026
It's not surprising to see Crow-Armstrong land the honor. He does just about everything well on the field.
As mentioned, he had a 40/40 season with 41 stolen bases and a league-leading 45 long balls. Speaking of leading the league, Crow-Armstrong also turned in the best marks in the National League with these statistics: 9.8 WAR (per Baseball Reference), 119 runs scored, .570 slugging percentage, .943 OPS, 156 OPS-plus and 357 total bases.
His Baseball Savant page will make the baseball analytic guys smile to say the least. His offensive rankings are beyond impressive. Meanwhile, he ranked in the 100th percentile for outs above average while playing a premier position in center field. He's also in the 93rd percentile in arm value and 90th percentile in arm strength.
As evidenced by his 41 steals, Crow-Armstrong also runs well. In fact, he's in the 95th percentile for sprint speed.
He's an incredible all-around player. The Cubs' goal is to win the World Series. While they fell short of that feat this year, Chicago will feel confident about its chances of reaching the Fall Classic in the near future with Baseball America's MLB Player of the Year leading the way.
